brief_summary:
This study will involve 27 centers in Italy. Since this is a multidisciplinary disease, participating centers may be from various medical areas (hematology, dermatology, allergy, etc.).

The study will last 10 years. The first patient is estimated to be enrolled in January 2021, while the last patient is expected to be completed in January 2031.

This is a retrospective and prospective registry. Since no intervention is foreseen, it can be considered an observational study.

The primary objective is to understand the clinical implications of mastocytosis, including the natural course of the disease, treatments and outcomes, variability in medical care, and disease burden.

Secondary objectives:

* To estimate the prevalence, incidence, and clinical course of mastocytosis
* To provide clinicians with prospective data to assist in the clinical management of individual patients
* To systematically collect data that can be integrated with data from other studies to support aggregate and comparative analyses.

Approximately 1,500 patients already treated at participating centers will be enrolled.

It is estimated that approximately 250-300 new patients will be included in the registry each year.

Patients ≥18 years of age and diagnosed with mastocytosis will be included in the study.

Each participant must be able to provide written informed consent to be enrolled.

There are no exclusion criteria. Variables to be collected. The study objectives will be assessed through data collection of the clinical and biological variables collected.
primary_outcomes: To develop an understanding of the longitudinal clinical implications of mastocytosis, including disease natural history, treatments and outcomes, and variability in clinical care and disease burden.
title: New Italian Mastocytosis Registry

brief_summary:
This study compared the effects of two running-based exercise programs on psychological distress, self-control, and emotion regulation in male university students who were not sufficiently physically active.

Thirty-six participants aged 18-25 years were randomly assigned to one of three groups: high-intensity interval training, moderate-intensity continuous training, or a wait-list control group. Both exercise programs lasted eight weeks and included three supervised sessions per week, for a total of 24 sessions. High-intensity interval training involved alternating periods of intense exercise and recovery, while moderate-intensity continuous training involved continuous exercise at a moderate intensity. The control group did not receive either exercise program during the study.

Participants completed questionnaires before and after the eight-week study period. The study examined whether changes in psychological distress, self-control, and emotion regulation differed among the three groups.
primary_outcomes: Change in Psychological Distress Measured by the 12-Item General Health Questionnaire (GHQ-12)
Change in Self-Control Measured by the 9-Item Brief Self-Control Scale (BSCS-9)
Change in Emotion Regulation Measured by the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ)
title: Effects of High-Intensity Interval Training and Moderate-Intensity Continuous Training on Psychological Distress and Self-Regulation in Insufficiently Active Male University Students

brief_summary:
The purpose of this randomized controlled trial is to compare the effectiveness of two topical combination treatments for mild-to-moderate acne vulgaris: 1% nadifloxacin with 0.025% tretinoin cream versus 1% clindamycin with 0.025% tretinoin cream. The study will be conducted in the Department of Dermatology, Nishtar Hospital, Multan, and will enroll adults aged 18 to 40 years of either gender who are newly diagnosed with mild-to-moderate acne vulgaris. Participants with drug-induced acne, endocrine disorders (such as PCOS), other chronic facial skin conditions, pregnancy or lactation, chronic systemic illness, or known hypersensitivity to the study medications will be excluded.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups, with allocation concealed using sealed opaque envelopes. Group A will apply nadifloxacin plus tretinoin cream, and Group B will apply clindamycin plus tretinoin cream. In both groups, a thin layer of the assigned cream will be applied once daily at bedtime to the whole affected area after washing the face with a mild cleanser. Participants will also be advised to use a non-comedogenic moisturizer and sunscreen and to avoid other acne treatments. Follow-up visits will take place at 4, 8, and 12 weeks, with medication use checked by inspecting returned tubes and side effects (redness, dryness, peeling, burning, itching, allergic reactions) recorded at each visit.

At baseline and after 12 weeks of treatment, a consultant dermatologist who is unaware of the treatment assigned will count inflammatory, non-inflammatory, and total lesions and grade acne severity using the Global Acne Grading System. The main outcome is the reduction in the number of inflammatory lesions after 12 weeks. Secondary outcomes are the reduction in non-inflammatory and total lesions, change in acne severity grade, and side effects.

The study hypothesizes that the reduction in inflammatory lesions at 12 weeks is greater with nadifloxacin plus tretinoin than with clindamycin plus tretinoin.
primary_outcomes: Reduction in number of inflammatory acne lesions
title: Comparing Nadifloxacin Plus Tretinoin Versus Clindamycin Plus Tretinoin Creams for Mild-to-Moderate Acne

brief_summary:
Lipedema is a chronic condition characterized by abnormal accumulation and distribution of adipose tissue, most commonly affecting the lower extremities, and may be associated with swelling, discomfort, reduced mobility, and changes in physical and emotional well-being. Although exercise and movement are commonly recommended as part of supportive care, there is limited clinical research examining whether a structured, remotely delivered mind-body chair yoga program can improve functional mobility in individuals with lipedema.

This study will evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of a remote mind-body chair yoga intervention on functional mobility in adults with lipedema. The study builds on a previous citizen-science quality-of-life yoga program and is designed to further evaluate the intervention using a prospective clinical research design.

Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to one of two groups. The intervention group will participate in a structured mind-body chair yoga program in addition to a weekly support group. The comparison group will participate in the weekly support group without yoga during the primary study period. After completion of the study, participants in the comparison group will be offered access to the chair yoga program.

The mind-body chair yoga intervention will be delivered remotely and will incorporate gentle chair-based yoga, breathing practices, relaxation, meditation, and other accessible mind-body practices. The program is designed to accommodate individuals with varying levels of mobility and physical ability and does not require participants to perform yoga poses on the floor.

The primary outcome of the study is functional mobility. Secondary outcomes will examine changes in lipedema symptom severity, pain, sleep, and mental well-being. Participant experiences and perceptions of the intervention will also be explored using qualitative measures.

The study will assess whether a remotely delivered mind-body chair yoga program is feasible for individuals with lipedema and whether participation is associated with improvements in functional mobility and other quality-of-life-related outcomes. Findings may help inform future research and the development of accessible mind-body movement programs for individuals living with lipedema.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility of the Remote Mind-Body Chair Yoga Intervention
title: Mind-Body Chair Yoga for Functional Mobility in Individuals With Lipedema

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate the effects of an upper extremity physiotherapy program combined with home exercises on activities of daily living, quality of life, joint range of motion, and pain in individuals with hemiplegia following stroke.

The study compares two groups: participants receiving supervised physiotherapy in addition to a home exercise program and participants performing a home exercise program only. The intervention includes stretching, range-of-motion exercises, arm ergometer training, progressive strengthening, coordination exercises, and fine motor activities.

The intervention period lasts 10 weeks. Outcomes are assessed using the Barthel Index, Short Form-36 (SF-36), Visual Analog Scale (VAS), goniometric measurements, and sensory assessments.

The study aims to evaluate whether adding supervised physiotherapy to home exercises provides additional benefits for upper extremity rehabilitation following stroke.
primary_outcomes: Change in Barthel Index Score
Change in SF-36 Quality of Life Scores
title: Effects of Upper Extremity Physiotherapy and Home Exercises on Functional Outcomes in Individuals With Stroke

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effects of eye covering and white noise during nasogastric tube insertion on comfort, pain, stress, and physiological parameters in preterm infants. A total of 90 preterm infants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: eye covering, white noise, or combined eye covering and white noise. Comfort, pain, stress, heart rate, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation will be assessed before, during, and after nasogastric tube insertion.
primary_outcomes: Neonatal Comfort Level Assessed Using the COMFORTneo Scale
title: Eye Covering and White Noise During Nasogastric Tube Insertion in Preterm Infants

brief_summary:
Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a long-term inflammatory disease that mainly affects the spine and sacroiliac joints, causing back pain and stiffness. Some patients do not respond well to existing treatments. This study will test an investigational cell therapy called GKL-006Allo injection, made from donor-derived invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells and given by intravenous infusion.

The study will evaluate two dose levels of GKL-006Allo, given once every two weeks for up to 11 doses. The study starts at a lower dose. After a safety review committee confirms the safety of the current dose level, the study may move to a higher dose. The main purposes are to find out how safe and well tolerated GKL-006Allo is, how it moves through the body (pharmacokinetics), whether it triggers an immune response (immunogenicity), and to collect early information on whether it improves AS.

Researchers will monitor participants for 52 weeks after the first dose to track safety and disease-related measures.

All participants completed a standardized 5-minute step exercise. HRV was assessed before exercise, immediately after exercise, and immediately after the assigned 10-minute recovery intervention. The study aimed to compare changes in cardiac autonomic recovery among the three recovery conditions.

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether two laboratory tests give the same results when measuring blood levels of blood thinners. The study looked at adults who take direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) and came to an emergency department. DOACs are blood thinners such as apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban and rivaroxaban.

Doctors do not usually measure DOAC levels in the blood. In an emergency, though, knowing the level can help doctors decide on treatment. This matters, for example, when a person is bleeding or has a blood clot.

The main questions the study aims to answer are:

* Do a standard hospital test and a more precise reference test give similar DOAC levels?
* How many participants have DOAC levels that are too low, normal or too high?
* Are levels that are too low or too high linked to emergency visits for bleeding or blood clots?

Participants:

* gave one blood sample when they arrived at the emergency department
* received their usual care, with no change to their treatment

Researchers measured the DOAC level in each sample with both tests. They also collected information from medical records, such as the reason for the visit and the time since the last DOAC dose.
primary_outcomes: Agreement between DOAC plasma concentrations measured by chromogenic assay and by HPLC-MS/MS
title: Plasma Concentration Monitoring of Direct Oral Anticoagulants in Emergency Department Patients: Comparison of Two Laboratory Methods

brief_summary:
This prospective observational study aims to evaluate and compare the interpretation of antenatal non-stress tests (NSTs) by three artificial intelligence models, three obstetricians, and three midwives.

A total of 300 NST recordings obtained during routine antenatal care will be collected and prepared in PDF format. The recordings will be distributed to the evaluators, who will independently assess NST reactivity and recommend appropriate clinical management within two weeks.

Two perinatologists will independently evaluate the NST recordings to establish the reference standard. In cases of disagreement, a third perinatologist will be consulted to determine the final reference assessment.

The study will compare the diagnostic performance, agreement with the reference standard, and inter-rater agreement among artificial intelligence models, obstetricians, and midwives.
primary_outcomes: Agreement in Non-Stress Test Classification
title: Artificial Intelligence, Obstetricians, and Midwives in Non-Stress Test Interpretation

brief_summary:
Gastric intestinal metaplasia (GIM) is a precancerous condition associated with an increased risk of gastric cancer. The endoscopic grading of gastric intestinal metaplasia (EGGIM) score evaluates the extent of GIM across five standard gastric regions. The investigators developed a real-time artificial intelligence-assisted EGGIM (AI-EGGIM) system that automatically assigns an intestinal metaplasia grade to each region and calculates a total EGGIM score.

This prospective multi-center validation study will consecutively enroll patients undergoing upper gastrointestinal endoscopy. The AI-EGGIM system will generate real-time grades for the five standard gastric regions. Regardless of endoscopic appearance or AI output, every patient will undergo five mapping biopsies, with one biopsy obtained from each standard region. Histopathological operative link on gastric intestinal metaplasia (OLGIM) staging will serve as the reference standard. The primary objective is to estimate the performance of an AI-EGGIM score ≥ 5 for identifying patients at high risk of gastric cancer.
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity of AI-EGGIM ≥ 5 for Identifying Patients at High Risk of Gastric Cancer
title: Multi-center Prospective Validation of Real-Time AI-EGGIM System

brief_summary: Lateral ankle sprains are common musculoskeletal injuries, particularly among young adults and athletes. Although recovery is often favorable, lateral ankle sprains may be associated with persistent pain, chronic ankle instability, delayed return to sport, and an increased risk of recurrence. The Ankle-GO score is a recently developed tool for assessing functional recovery after a lateral ankle sprain. Available data mainly concern assessments performed from the second month after injury onward. To our knowledge, changes in this score during the early recovery phase have not yet been evaluated. The ASGO study aims to describe changes in the Ankle-GO score in patients enrolled early after a lateral ankle sprain and followed for four months.
lead_sponsor: Groupe Hospitalier de la Rochelle Ré Aunis
primary_outcomes: Total Ankle-GO score measured at M2
title: Functional Recovery After a Recent Lateral Ankle Sprain With Early Initiation of Rehabilitation: Changes in the Ankle-GO Score and Its Association With Return to Sport and Recurrent Sprains.

brief_summary: This study is for adult participants with moderate to severe Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) who continue to experience exacerbations despite standard of care triple therapy treatment. It will assess the effectiveness and safety of two investigational drugs, GSK3862995B and GSK5784283, given together compared to a placebo in addition to standard of care.

brief_summary:
This study will compare how young adults respond to four audiovisual artworks inspired by ice melt and permafrost thaw in Nunavik, northern Quebec. Permafrost is ground that remains frozen for at least two consecutive years. The researchers want to understand whether the artworks evoke different emotions, bodily responses and personal interpretations, and whether they help make environmental changes more concrete and meaningful.

The four artworks draw on the same 30 years of environmental data from the Tasiujaq area of Nunavik. They combine music and moving images through different creative approaches:

1. Contemporary music created by a human composer, paired with images generated using artificial intelligence (AI).
2. Inuit pop-rock music created independently by an Inuk artist, paired with AI-generated images.
3. Music and images generated using AI from the environmental data.
4. AI-generated music combining and reworking material from the two human-created compositions, paired with AI-generated images.

The study will recruit 80 adults aged 18-35 who understand French or English and can provide informed consent. It will take place at the Research Centre of the Montreal Geriatric University Institute in Montreal, Quebec, Canada.

Before attending, participants will complete approximately 30 minutes of online questionnaires about their background, connection with nature, environmental concerns, and familiarity with music, Inuit culture, Nunavik and AI. They will then attend one laboratory session lasting approximately 60 minutes.

During the session, every participant will watch and listen to all four artworks. Each artwork lasts 3 minutes and 50 seconds. Participants will be assigned to one of eight presentation orders to reduce the influence of viewing order on their responses. Viewing conditions will be kept consistent, and the artworks will be presented under neutral labels.

Before each artwork, participants will sit quietly for approximately one minute while resting physiological measurements are recorded. Sensors will measure changes in skin conductance, which reflects changes in sweating, and heart rate during viewing. These measurements will be considered alongside participants' own reports because they cannot, by themselves, identify a specific emotion.

Participants will complete short questionnaires before and after each artwork about how pleasant or unpleasant they feel, how calm or activated they feel, and specific positive and negative emotions. Further questions will explore their appreciation and interpretation of the artworks and the responses the works evoke. After viewing all four, participants will repeat questionnaires about nature connectedness and environmental anxiety, compare the artworks, and explain their choices in their own words.

The researchers will compare responses to the four artworks within each participant and explore whether responses are associated with individual characteristics, including initial environmental concerns and familiarity with the arts or AI. Each artwork will be evaluated as a complete experience. Differences cannot be attributed separately to musical style, cultural references or the use of AI.

This study is not a treatment for anxiety or another health condition, and no direct health benefit is guaranteed. Participants may request a break or stop the session at any time.
conditions: Emotional, Affective, and Physiological Responses to Audiovisual Artworks Inspired by Climate-Related Environmental Changes in Nunavik
interventions: Viewing Four Audiovisual Artworks Inspired by Environmental Changes in Nunavik
lead_sponsor: Centre integre universitaire de sante et de services sociaux du Centre-Sud-de-l'Île-de-Montréal
primary_outcomes: Change in Affect Grid Valence Score Following Each Audiovisual Artwork
Change in Affect Grid Arousal Score Following Each Audiovisual Artwork
Electrodermal Responses During Audiovisual Artwork Viewing
Heart Rate Responses During Audiovisual Artwork Viewing
title: Emotional and Affective Responses to Music Inspired by Permafrost Thaw in Nunavik

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether the combination of trigonelline and sufentanil can better control postoperative pain in adult women undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery, while reducing discomforts such as nausea and vomiting. It also aims to explore whether using both drugs together is safer than using either one alone.

The main questions it seeks to answer are:

Does trigonelline combined with sufentanil result in less pain for participants after surgery? Does the combination reduce the occurrence of nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and other side effects?

Researchers will compare three different postoperative pain relief plans to determine which one works best and causes the fewest side effects:

Sufentanil group: receiving only sufentanil (a commonly used strong pain-relieving medicine) Trigonelline group: receiving only trigonelline (a newer type of pain-relieving medicine that may cause fewer stomach problems) Combination group: receiving both medicines together, each at half the usual dose

Participants will:

Sign an informed consent form before surgery agreeing to take part in this study Receive pain relief through a patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) pump connected to a vein in the hand or arm after surgery (the pump can deliver medicine automatically, and participants may also press a button to request extra doses) Be asked by the medical team about their pain level at several time points within 48 hours after surgery Tell the researchers if they feel any discomfort such as nausea, dizziness, sleepiness, or itching
primary_outcomes: Visual Analog Scale (VAS) Pain Score at Rest and During Movement
title: Trigonelline Plus Sufentanil for Postoperative Analgesia After Laparoscopic Hysterectomy: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial

brief_summary: This prospective, multicenter, intraindividual paired study aims to evaluate the autonomous scanning performance of a dual-arm robotic breast ultrasound system and the diagnostic performance of the images it acquires, in comparison with conventional handheld ultrasound. The study primarily focuses on the agreement between diagnostic assessments based on images obtained using the two examination methods, while also evaluating image quality, lesion detection, and measurement performance. The robotic ultrasound findings will be collected for research purposes only and will not be used to guide clinical management; all clinical decisions will be based on routine clinical assessment.

brief_summary: Postoperative neurocognitive disorders, including postoperative delirium (POD) and delayed neurocognitive recovery (dNCR), are common in older patients undergoing surgery and are associated with worse outcomes. Intranasal dexmedetomidine, esketamine, and their combination have been used in clinical practice to improve sleep quality and analgesia. A preliminary study suggested lower rates of emergence delirium and POD/dNCR in older patients receiving perioperative intranasal dexmedetomidine-esketamine. This randomized controlled trial is designed to test the hypothesis that perioperative administration of an intranasal dexmedetomidine-esketamine combination improves neurocognitive recovery in older patients undergoing noncardiac surgery.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of delayed neurocognitive recovery (dNCR) on postoperative day 4.

brief_summary:
This observational study will investigate whether problematic digital media use is associated with anxiety in children undergoing a planned upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, a camera examination of the upper digestive tract. The study hypothesis is that problematic media use is associated with the child's anxiety immediately before sedation. Associations with sedation medicine requirements and recovery after the procedure will also be explored.

The study will include 60 children aged 6 to 11 years. Parents or legal guardians will complete a questionnaire about their child's media use and provide information on screen time and viewing habits. An independent observer will assess anxiety at three time points: on arrival in the preparation area, before transfer to the procedure room, and immediately before sedation.

Researchers will record the medicines and doses used for sedation or anaesthesia, procedure duration, agitation during recovery, recovery time, readiness for discharge, and sedation-related adverse events. Endoscopy and sedation will be managed according to routine clinical practice.
primary_outcomes: Modified Yale Preoperative Anxiety Scale (mYPAS) scores
title: Media Use, Anxiety, Sedation, and Recovery in Children Having Upper GI Endoscopy

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to find out which treatment best preserves the jawbone after tooth extraction in adults planning to receive a dental implant later.

The study will investigate whether adding vitamin C to a mixture of tooth particles and a material prepared from the participant's own blood helps preserve the jawbone and improve bone healing.

The main questions it aims to answer are

* Does adding vitamin C help preserve the width of the jawbone after tooth extraction?
* Does it improve new bone formation compared with the other treatments?

Researchers will compare three treatments to determine whether adding a blood-based material, with or without vitamin C, improves bone preservation.

1. The first group will receive small particles prepared from their own extracted tooth.
2. The second group will receive tooth particles mixed with a healing material prepared from their own blood.
3. The third group will receive tooth particles mixed with the same blood-based material containing vitamin C.

Participants will undergo tooth extraction and receive one of these treatments. They will attend follow-up visits during the healing period.

Researchers will:

* Examine the treated area during follow-up visits.
* Take three-dimensional dental scans before treatment and four months later to measure changes in jawbone width and height.
* Collect a small bone sample during dental implant placement to examine new bone formation and healing.

The study will help determine whether adding vitamin C to the blood-based material provides additional benefits for preserving the jawbone before dental implant placement.

brief_summary:
Acute Kidney Injury is a serious, common illness that is associated with poor health outcomes. Prolonged hospitalisation is a common experience of patients admitted with this illness. The average hospital stay for patients with an acute kidney injury is approximately 12 days, which can have a significant impact on muscle mass, muscle strength and, as a result, physical function and quality of life after leaving hospital. These losses in muscle mass, strength and physical function are thought to be, at least in part, due to muscle disuse, which may be down to complex underlying mechanisms associated with the condition, but also due to the period of immobilisation and/or limited mobility during hospitalisation that most patients experience.

Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation or NMES, is an alternative, passive form of exercise that this study will use to: 1) test whether this is a feasible treatment option for patients with acute kidney injury; 2) observe whether it can be used to maintain or improve muscle mass, strength, and physical function; and 3) test whether there is any impact on quality of life or the ability to engage with activities of daily living after being discharged from hospital.

NMES is done by attaching pads to the skin of the leg muscles which send electrical impulses to the nerves, which then causes muscles to contract involuntarily. NMES has been shown to improve strength in the leg muscles, as well as physical function and tolerance to exercise by mimicking voluntary muscle contractions in the muscle that is stimulated. This small study will help us to gain an understanding on how patients respond to NMES whilst in hospital and inform the design of future larger studies on the use of NMES in acute kidney injury patients.
primary_outcomes: Number of patients screened
What proportion of people screened were eligible to take part?
What proportion of the eligible participants that were approached, were recruited?
title: Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation to Improve the Muscle Health of Individuals With Acute Kidney Injury

brief_summary: The incidence of accidental dural puncture (ADP) among parturients receiving neuraxial labor analgesia has been reported to range from 1% to 1.5%. Post-dural puncture headache (PDPH) is a headache caused by low cerebrospinal fluid pressure resulting from substantial cerebrospinal fluid leakage after dural and arachnoid puncture. Epidural filling with hydroxyethyl starch (HES) via an epidural catheter has been used to prevent PDPH in patients with ADP. This multicenter prospective cohort study aimed to evaluate the effect of epidural HES filling in preventing PDPH in parturients who experienced ADP during epidural labor analgesia or neuraxial anesthesia for cesarean delivery.
conditions: Accidental Puncture of Dura During Anaesthesia
primary_outcomes: Incidence of post-dural puncture headache (PDPH) within 7 days.
title: Epidural Hydroxyethyl Starch for Post-Dural Puncture Headache in Parturients

brief_summary: IMMUNOTIME is a French multicenter randomised phase III trial in patients with metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer starting first-line treatment with pembrolizumab, carboplatin and pemetrexed. Patients receive the standard regimen and are randomised to start their pembrolizumab infusions either in the morning (08:00-12:00) or in the afternoon (13:00-17:00). The trial aims to determine whether morning administration improves survival at one year. A total of 242 patients will be included in 33 centres.
primary_outcomes: Survival rate
title: Evaluation of the Effect of Time of Administration on the Activity on First Line of Pembrolizumab in Association With Carboplatin-pemetrexed in Metastatic Non-squamous Lung Cancer. A Randomised Multicenter Phase III Trial

brief_summary:

Evaluation criterion: statistical association between biological markers and the occurrence of glucocorticoid complications.

Glucocorticoid-related complications are collected in a research program called "CDE.AI" (common data elements, artificial intelligence). CDE.AI aims at processing unstructured medical reports with natural language processing tools to fill in automatically forms reporting the outcome of patients with glucoocorticoid excess.

brief_summary:
This study compared the effects of guided mindfulness and breathing exercises on mindfulness, self-esteem, and anxiety in university students. Mindfulness means paying attention to present-moment experiences without judgment. The researchers expected both programs to improve mindfulness and self-esteem and reduce anxiety compared with continuing usual daily activities.

The study included three groups: a mindfulness group, a breathing exercise group, and a no-intervention control group. Students in the two intervention groups attended face-to-face group sessions lasting 20-25 minutes each day for five days. The control group continued usual daily activities without receiving a study intervention.

Questionnaires were completed before and immediately after the five-day study period. These assessed mindfulness, self-esteem, anxiety at the time of assessment, the general tendency to experience anxiety, and examination-related anxiety. Changes were compared across the three groups.
primary_outcomes: Change in Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire-Short Form (FFMQ-SF) Total Score
title: Effects of Mindfulness and Breathing Exercises in University Students

brief_summary:
This study was designed to examine the effects of a three-week mobile video game intervention on visual reaction time and basketball free-throw performance in healthy young adults. Fifty participants were assigned to either an experimental group or a control group.

Participants in the experimental group completed a mobile video game intervention using Basketball Stars and PUBG Mobile for three weeks, three days per week, with a total of 30 minutes of gaming on each intervention day. Participants in the control group continued their usual daily activities during the study period.

Visual reaction time was designated as the primary outcome and basketball free-throw performance as the secondary outcome. Both outcomes were assessed at baseline and after the three-week intervention period. The study was conducted using a non-randomized controlled pretest-posttest design.

brief_summary:
Schizophrenia is a chronic mental health disorder that affects thinking, emotions, behavior, and quality of life. Although antipsychotic medications such as risperidone are commonly used to manage schizophrenia, some patients continue to experience psychiatric symptoms and reduced quality of life. Inflammation may also contribute to the development and severity of schizophrenia.

Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) is a medicinal plant with potential anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties. This study evaluated whether adding ashwagandha to standard risperidone treatment could improve quality of life, reduce psychiatric symptoms, and lower blood levels of tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), a marker of inflammation, in patients with schizophrenia.

This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study included 60 male patients with schizophrenia aged 20 to 45 years. Participants were randomly assigned to receive either ashwagandha plus risperidone or placebo plus risperidone for eight weeks.

Quality of life, psychiatric symptoms, and blood levels of TNF-alpha were assessed at the beginning of the study and after eight weeks of treatment. The study aimed to provide additional evidence regarding the potential benefits of ashwagandha as an adjunctive treatment for schizophrenia.
primary_outcomes: Change in Serum TNF-alpha Concentration From Baseline to Week 8
title: Ashwagandha Added to Risperidone for Quality of Life and Inflammation in Schizophrenia

brief_summary: This prospective, open-label, randomized clinical study will evaluate the effect of empagliflozin 10 mg daily, added to standard T2DM treatment, on liver fat and hepatic parameters in adults with type 2 diabetes and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease. Two hundred eligible participants will be randomized 1:1 to empagliflozin plus standard therapy or standard therapy alone and followed for 12 weeks. The primary outcome is change in liver fat assessed by liver ultrasonography. Secondary outcomes include changes in ALT, AST, AST/ALT ratio, AP index, APRI, FIB-4, NFS, and BARD scores.
interventions: Empagliflozin 10/15 mg administered orally once daily in addition to standard treatment for type 2 diabetes mellitus.

Change in liver fat
title: Effect of Empagliflozin on Liver Fat in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease

brief_summary: Heart failure is a chronic health condition associated with high morbidity and hospital readmission rates, negatively affecting patients' self-care behaviors, physical activity levels, and quality of life. Although cardiac rehabilitation programs offer significant benefits, the sustainability of self-care behaviors in the home environment remains a major challenge. There is a limited number of theory-based intervention studies that integrate components such as spousal support, structured education, and telemonitoring. This study aims to examine the impact of an intervention-structured according to Imogene King's Theory of Goal Attainment and incorporating spousal support, education, and telemonitoring-on the self-care behaviors and physical activity levels of patients with heart failure during their rehabilitation process. The study will be conducted as a randomized controlled trial with a pre-test/post-test control group design. The sample will consist of patients with NYHA Class II-III heart failure who are enrolled in a cardiac rehabilitation program. Ethical approval and institutional authorization will be obtained prior to the study. At the outset, all participants will undergo a pre-test, and their sociodemographic and clinical data will be assessed. The intervention group will receive face-to-face education during the first two weeks to initiate a goal-setting process, followed by weekly video-based educational modules over the next six weeks. Throughout this period, patients' symptoms, weight, medication adherence, and physical activity levels will be monitored via WhatsApp-based telemonitoring and weekly telephone calls. An interim assessment will be conducted at the sixth week; the intervention will span a total of 12 weeks, concluding with a post-test at the 12th week. The control group will receive only routine care. The video educational modules will be prepared in alignment with the current ESC and AHA/ACC/HFSA guidelines and developed using AI-powered digital tools, such as Google Flow and NotebookLM. Data will be collected using the European Heart Failure Self-Care Behaviour Scale, the International Physical Activity Questionnaire, the Perceived Partner Responsiveness Scale, and a Weekly Goal and Data Tracking Form. The study is expected to contribute to the development of a feasible and sustainable nursing care approach within the cardiac rehabilitation process.
primary_outcomes: Change in Self-Care Behaviors
Change in Total Physical Activity (MET-minutes/week)
Change in Physical Activity Classification
Change in Daily Sitting Time (minutes/day)
title: King's Theory-Based Multicomponent Interventions in Heart Failure Patient Rehabilitation

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial compared the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT) on physiological and functional outcomes in physically trained adults aged 18-35 years. A total of 46 participants were assigned to two exercise groups. Both groups followed an eight-week supervised cycling program, with three 30-minute sessions per week. Assessments were conducted at baseline, week 4, and week 8. The study evaluated estimated aerobic capacity, anaerobic performance, postural balance, pulmonary function, and heart rate variability to determine how these outcomes respond to different exercise intensities.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Estimated Maximal Oxygen Uptake (VO2max)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a probiotic supplement can improve symptoms and quality of life in adults with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) or functional diarrhea (FD). These conditions can cause frequent loose stools, abdominal discomfort, and a lower quality of life.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does the probiotic improve quality of life compared with a placebo (a look-alike capsule that contains no active bacteria)?
* Does the probiotic help participants have more normal stool consistency and fewer bowel movements?
* Is the probiotic safe and well tolerated in people with IBS-D or FD?

Researchers will compare the probiotic supplement with a placebo to see whether the probiotic improves symptoms and quality of life.

Participants will:

* Take either the probiotic or placebo capsule once daily for 3 months.
* Switch to the other study treatment for an additional 3 months.
* Complete quality-of-life questionnaires at the start of the study, after 3 months, and after 6 months.
* Record the number of bowel movements each day throughout the study.
* Record stool consistency each day using the Bristol Stool Form Scale.
* Record daily pain during bowel movements using a Visual Analog Scale (VAS).
* Report any medications they take and any health problems that occur during the study.

The study will follow each participant for 6 months. Researchers hope the results will help determine whether this probiotic is a useful treatment option for people living with IBS-D or functional diarrhea.
primary_outcomes: Irritable Bowel Syndrome Quality of Life (IBS-QOL) Total Score at 3 Months
title: Lactic Acid Bacteria in Functional Diarrheal Disorders

brief_summary:
High blood pressure often occurs together with abnormal blood glucose, abnormal blood lipids, or abdominal obesity. Managing these conditions outside the hospital can be difficult. This study will test whether a digital health program that combines artificial intelligence (AI) with review and support by doctors and nurses improves health outcomes compared with standard out-of-hospital guidance.

The study will enroll 150 adults aged 18 to 70 years who have hypertension and at least one additional cardiometabolic risk factor that is not at target. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the hybrid AI-assisted management group or the standard-guidance group. The intervention group will use a patient mini-program and connected devices to monitor blood pressure, glucose, and lifestyle information. The AI system will propose personalized medication, diet, exercise, and monitoring plans, which the healthcare team will review and confirm before delivery. The control group will receive routine printed health education and usual clinical follow-up.

All participants will be followed for 6 months. The main outcome is the proportion of participants achieving blood pressure control together with control of at least one glycemic or lipid indicator. Other assessments include treatment adherence, cardiovascular events, hospitalizations, medical costs, quality of life, and system usability.
lead_sponsor: China National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants Achieving Blood Pressure Control and Control of at Least One Glycemic or Lipid Indicator
Composite Treatment and Health-Management Adherence
title: Multimodal AI-Driven Out-of-Hospital Management for Hypertension and Cardiometabolic Risk

brief_summary:
Population aging is transforming the epidemiological landscape of the Asia-Pacific region at an unprecedented pace. By 2050, more than one quarter of the region's population will be aged over 60, with 36.7% of countries projected to become" super-aged" societies.

Within Hong Kong specifically, the age- and gender-adjusted prevalence rates of mild and major neurocognitive disorder (NCD) among adults aged 60 years or above have been estimated at 21.8% and 9.7%, respectively. The scale of this burden intensifies considerably within institutional care environments, where roughly seven in ten long-term care (LTC) residents have been identified as having major NCD. Recent local survey data also indicate that severe cognitive impairment affects up to 49.8% of residents aged above 85 years. Given current demographic trajectories, the number of individuals living with dementia in Hong Kong is projected to triple over the next two decades. These trends underscore an urgent, time-sensitive need for scalable, accurate, and population-appropriate tools for the early detection and prognostic stratification of cognitive impairment, tools that must be actionable at the point of care and deployable at population scale.

This study aim to generate a large database of cognitive, neuroimaging, plasma biomarkers, lifestyle and psychological information of the subjects who suffered from neurocognitive disorders
primary_outcomes: Hong Kong Montreal Cognitive Assessment (HK-MoCA)
Clinical Dementia Rating
Hong Kong List Learning Test
Simple Mild Neurocognitive Disorder due to Alzheimer's Disease Risk Test (SMART)
title: Chinese University-Alzheimer's Disease With Vascular and Other Co-pathology: Towards Actionable Neuro-Cognitive-Omic Evaluations (CU-ADVANCE)

Because pediatric intubation is a high-risk, low-frequency procedure, simulation provides a safe environment for developing and assessing airway management skills. The study will assess providers' baseline experience and confidence, evaluate improvements following training, and examine confidence retention at six months.

brief_summary:
This prospective, single-center observational cohort study aims to investigate the feasibility, reproducibility, and longitudinal trajectory patterns of left ventricular myocardial work in adult patients with sepsis during the early phase of intensive care unit (ICU) treatment.

A total of 215 patients will be enrolled. Myocardial work indices, including global work efficiency (GWE), global work index (GWI), global constructive work (GCW), and global wasted work (GWW), will be assessed at approximately 12, 24, and 72 hours after ICU admission. Latent trajectory classes of GWE will be explored, and their internal stability will be evaluated.

The association between GWE trajectory classes and organ support-free days through day 28 will be assessed in a prespecified 84-hour landmark population. All treatment decisions will be made independently by the clinical team, and study-derived myocardial work measurements will not guide clinical management.
primary_outcomes: Organ Support-Free Days Through Day 28
title: Longitudinal Trajectories of Myocardial Work in Patients With Sepsis

brief_summary:
he main objective of this study is to compare the impact of two different file motions-continuous rotation versus reciprocation-using the same endodontic file system (MG3 Blue rotary files) on postoperative pain and the amount of remaining bacteria inside the root canal in single-rooted teeth with necrotic pulps.

Extrusion of infected debris and persistent intracanal bacteria during root canal treatment can lead to postoperative pain and treatment complications. While various instrumentation systems have been evaluated, differences in file metallurgy, design, and number of files often obscure whether the observed outcomes are due to the movement (kinematics) or the file itself. This study aims to isolate the effect of motion kinematics by using identical rotary files in two distinct movement modes.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups:

Intervention Group (Reciprocation Motion): Canals will be prepared using MG3 Blue files operated in reciprocation motion.

Comparator Group (Continuous Rotation Motion): Canals will be prepared using MG3 Blue files operated in continuous rotation motion.

All procedures will be performed on single-rooted mandibular premolars diagnosed with pulp necrosis without apical periodontitis. Microbial samples will be collected before and after canal instrumentation to measure the reduction of cultivable bacteria (in colony-forming units, CFU/mL). Postoperative pain levels will be recorded by participants using a Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) at baseline, 24 hours, 48 hours, 72 hours, and 7 days after the first appointment.

The primary outcome of the study is post-instrumentation pain at 72 hours. Secondary outcomes include post-instrumentation pain at 7 days and the amount of remaining intracanal cultivable bacteria following canal preparation.
conditions: Necrotic Pulps With no Apical Periodontitis
interventions: Engine driven files utilized in reciprocation motion
engine driven rotary files utilized in continuous rotation motion
primary_outcomes: post operative pain
title: Influence of Continuous Rotation Versus Reciprocation Motion of MG3 Blue Rotary File on Postoperative Pain and Intracanal Bacterial Reduction of Teeth With Necrotic Pulps.

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, open-label, randomized controlled clinical study. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Hepatic Arterial Infusion Chemotherapy (HAIC) compared with Capecitabine monotherapy as adjuvant therapy for patients with biliary tract cancer after radical resection.

Patients with histologically confirmed biliary tract cancer (including intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, and gallbladder cancer) who have undergone R0 or R1 resection will be enrolled. A total of approximately 90 eligible patients will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either HAIC (Oxaliplatin plus 5-Fluorouracil) or Capecitabine.

The primary endpoint is Recurrence-Free Survival (RFS). The secondary endpoints include Overall Survival (OS) and safety profiles. This study aims to provide high-level evidence for a more effective adjuvant treatment strategy to reduce recurrence and improve survival for patients with resected biliary tract cancer.
primary_outcomes: Recurrence-Free Survival (RFS)
title: Hepatic Arterial Infusion Chemotherapy Versus Capecitabine as Adjuvant Therapy for Resected Biliary Tract Cancer

brief_summary: This randomized 2×2 factorial study will examine how verbal expectancy framing and mindfulness-specific practice instructions influence acute pain and brain activity in adults with chronic pain. Sixty meditation-naïve adults will be assigned to one of four conditions combining positive or negative expectancy framing with either a guided mindfulness exercise or a sham-meditation comparison exercise. Pain intensity, pain unpleasantness, anxiety, desire for pain medication, and mindfulness-related psychological states will be assessed before and immediately after the intervention, while electroencephalography (EEG) will be used to measure changes in brain activity during the exercise. The study is designed to clarify the independent and combined contributions of expectancy and mindfulness-specific instructions to acute pain relief and neurophysiological responses.

Pain Unpleasantness

brief_summary:
Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) pump flow is typically calculated according to body surface area (BSA) derived from actual body weight and temperature, following the 2024 European guidelines recommending an indexed flow of 2.4 L/min/m². However, in obese patients, using actual weight leads to a high BSA and thus elevated pump flow, increasing technical challenges such as the need for larger cannulas, higher circulating blood volume, and elevated pump speeds. These adjustments may increase risks of hemodilution, transfusion, and hemolysis. Given that lean body mass in obese patients is similar to that of non-obese patients of the same height-and that aerobic metabolism depends on lean mass-adjusting CPB flow based on ideal body weight rather than actual weight could reduce transfusions and associated complications. Several observational studies support the concept of using ideal body weight for CPB flow calculation in obese patients. Despite this, no randomized controlled trial has yet addressed the clinical impact of this approach. Given the increasing prevalence of obesity and the practical challenges it poses during cardiac surgery, a controlled clinical trial is warranted.

The investigators hypothesize that adjusting the cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) flow according to the ideal body weight rather than the actual body weight in obese patients could reduce the need for blood transfusions and limit the associated complications.
primary_outcomes: reduction in the incidence of erythrocyte concentrates transfused
title: Optimized Cardiopulmonary Bypass Flow Strategy Based on Ideal Body Weight in Obese Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery

brief_summary:
Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a common side effect of certain types of chemotherapy and can cause numbness, tingling, pain, and other symptoms in the hands and feet. There is currently no established method for preventing CIPN.

The purpose of this randomized controlled trial is to investigate whether continuous, controlled cooling of the hands and feet during chemotherapy can reduce the development and severity of CIPN. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either cooling with the Hilotherm device during chemotherapy or standard care without cooling.

The study will compare peripheral neuropathy between the two groups and assess whether continuous cooling can help prevent chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy.
interventions: Continuous Controlled Cooling of the Hands and Feet
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Clinically Meaningful Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy
title: Continuous Controlled Cooling for Prevention of Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy

brief_summary:
Female Genital Schistosomiasis (FGS) is a neglected complication of Schistosoma haematobium infection affecting an estimated 56 million women and girls globally, with a high burden in sub-Saharan Africa. Up to 75% of infected women develop genital lesions, often without being aware of their condition. FGS causes chronic genital and urinary symptoms, overlaps clinically with sexually transmitted infections, and increases the risk of HIV acquisition by 2-4 times. FGS remains widely underdiagnosed due to limited healthcare provider training, stigma, and lack of affordable diagnostic tools in resource-limited settings. Current control strategies rely on mass drug administration of praziquantel (PZQ) targeting school-aged children and adults in high risk or endemic communities, which neither adequately reaches affected women nor addresses established genital morbidity. PZQ eliminates adult worms but does not reverse chronic inflammation or granulomas caused by trapped eggs, and no clinical guidelines exist for managing FGS-related morbidity. Given these gaps, there is an urgent need to evaluate additional, locally available treatments in combination with praziquantel to reduce inflammation, improve morbidity outcomes, and inform effective clinical management of FGS.

This trial is funded by Global Health EDCTP3 and sponsored by KUHeS, INRB, UFHB, and UHAS. This Phase III, open label, 4x2 factorial superiority randomized controlled trial will take place in multiple schistosomiasis endemic countries in sub-Saharan Africa, among women living with schistosomiasis, testing already registered anti-inflammatory drugs (prednisolone, diclofenac). Each arm shall have at least 100 participants, who shall be followed up at 3-, 6-, and 12-month post first IP administration.

The trial will recruit 800 girls and women of reproductive age (15- 49 years) at 4 sites (Malawi, Ghana, Democratic Republic of Congo, and Cote d'Ivoire), with each site aiming to recruit 200 participants (25 per site per treatment arm).
primary_outcomes: Improvement in pathognomonic sign(s) in the cervix from baseline to month 3.
Improvement (reduction) in urogenital frequency symptom score from baseline to month 3.
title: A Phase III Trial to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Anti-inflammatory Drugs in Addition to Praziquantel in Girls and Women With Female Genital Schistosomiasis

Is ChatGPT as effective as supervised pain education? brief_summary: Participants with chronic low back pain will be randomly allocated to three groups: conservative treatment, conservative treatment plus local myofascial release, or conservative treatment plus superficial back line myofascial release. All groups will receive treatment three times weekly for six weeks. The conservative treatment program will include stretching, strengthening, and postural exercises. Myofascial release will be performed using a roller bar, with controlled rhythmic pressure applied for 30-60 seconds per region, totaling 10-15 minutes per session, according to individual tolerance. Age, height, weight, and body mass index will be recorded. Outcomes will include pain intensity (Visual Analog Scale), pressure pain threshold (digital algometer), range of motion (goniometer), static and dynamic balance (Biodex Balance System), and functional disability (Oswestry Disability Index). All outcomes will be assessed before and after the intervention.

brief_summary:
Medical students often experience high levels of stress, anxiety, and poor sleep, especially during their first year and around exams. This study looked at whether adding hands-on osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) to a wellness program built around a wearable ring and an artificial intelligence (AI) health coaching app could help first-year medical students.

Forty-three first-year osteopathic medical students at one college took part. Each student was randomly assigned, by chance rather than by choice, to one of three groups for 23 weeks: a wearable ring alone; a wearable ring plus an AI health coaching app; or a wearable ring, the AI health coaching app, and seven OMT sessions given about every three weeks by osteopathic physicians.

All students wore the ring daily. The ring recorded information such as sleep, heart rate, and heart rate variability, which is a measure of how the nervous system responds to stress. Students also completed questionnaires about resilience and about symptoms of depression, anxiety, and stress at three points: before the semester, in the middle, and at the end. Students answered additional surveys about their experience two months and seven months after the study ended.

This was a small pilot study. Its main purpose was to find out whether a program like this can be carried out successfully and to gather the information needed to plan a larger study, rather than to determine whether OMT works. No harmful effects were reported.
interventions: Wearable ring with continuous biometric monitoring
primary_outcomes: Change in resilience, measured by the Hardiness Resilience Gauge (HRG) Total Hardiness T-score
Change in mood symptoms, measured by the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21)
title: High-Tech, High-Touch

brief_summary:
This Phase 1, randomized, double-blind study is designed to evaluate safety, tolerability, PK, and PD effects of AB-110. This study will be conducted in 2 parts: a single ascending dose (SAD; Part A) in healthy participants with an optional cohort of BMI \> 30 kg/m2 and ≤ 35 kg/m2 and multiple ascending dose (MAD; Part B) in participants with hypertension who are otherwise healthy. Sentinel dosing will be applied in the Part A study at each new dose level to ensure participant's safety.

The study will provide initial insight into the safety and tolerability of AB-110. In addition to safety, the study is designed to enable insights on secondary and exploratory research questions, including Blood Pressure (BP) reduction and exploratory biomarkers.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Adverse Events and Serious Adverse Events, overall, by severity and relationship to AB-110/placebo
Incidence of injection site reactions
title: Study of AB-110 in Healthy and Hypertensive Participants

brief_summary:
This single-arm, open-label pilot study aims to evaluate changes in ovarian function following administration of autologous hair follicle-derived mesenchymal stem cell secretome combined with autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) in women with premature ovarian insufficiency (POI).

The study plans to enroll 15 women aged 25-40 years with evidence of diminished ovarian activity, including elevated follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), low anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), and reduced antral follicle count (AFC).

The intervention is administered under transvaginal ultrasound guidance into the pelvic cul-de-sac, without direct ovarian injection. Participants undergo serial hormonal and ultrasound assessments to evaluate changes in FSH, AMH, and AFC. Secondary assessments include menstrual function, ovulation, and pregnancy outcomes.

The study is exploratory and is intended to generate preliminary data on ovarian response, feasibility, and safety to inform future controlled investigations.
interventions: Autologous Hair Follicle-Derived Secretome Combined With Platelet-Rich Plasma

Change in Serum Anti-Müllerian Hormone Levels
Change in Antral Follicle Count

brief_summary:
Background:

Psoriasis is a chronic , immune-mediated inflammatory skin disorder affecting millions globally, the disease presents a major challenge to the physicians. When choosing a systemic therapy for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis, methotrexate is very good option, though its use is limited by its adverse effects. Several new treatments for psoriasis have appeared to be effective though they are not adequately investigated. Among them JAK inhibitors are leading clinical trials and can be a breakthrough in the treatment of psoriasis. Moreover, Very few studies have been performed to compare efficacy and safety of Deucravacitinib with Methotrexate therapy in the treatment of psoriasis.

Objective:

To assess Efficacy and Safety after commencement of therapy with Deucravacitinib and Methotrexate therapy in two different groups of patients with psoriasis.

Materials and Methods:

The study will be done on patients aged more than 18 years attending outpatient Department of Dermatology and Venereology department of Bangladesh Medical University.

This will be a longitudinal study. It will be conducted in the Department of Dermatology and Venereology of Bangladesh Medical University for 12 months from the acceptance of the protocol. Patients of psoriasis with PASI (Psoriasis Area and Severity Index) score 12 or more will be the study population. A total number 106 patients with psoriasis of both sexes will be enrolled. They will be divided in group A (53 patients) and group B (53 patients) according to inclusion and exclusion criteria In group A, patients will be treated with Deucravacitinib 6mg once daily for 6 months and efficacy will be assessed by PASI (Psoriasis Area and Severity Index) score periodically. In Group B, patients will be treated with Methotrexate 10 mg once weekly at night after meal, with folic acid 5mg tablet the day after taking methotrexate and efficacy will be assessed using PASI scoring tool. Finally efficacy and safety of two treatment modalities will be compared. Statistical analysis will be done with Chi square test, Fisher's exact test and multivariate linear regression for intergroup comparison safety assessment will be done on the basis of clinical history, examination and laboratory finding at each follow up. Adverse events will be explained to the patients. Ethical clearance will be obtained from Institutional Review Board of Bangladesh Medical University.

Ethical Consideration:

The nature and purpose of the study will be informed in details to all the participants. Before obtaining the consent, patients will be explained about the purpose and duration of the study, detailed study procedure, the benefits and potential risks (if any) involved with the study. Relevant investigations and therapeutic treatment will be given free of cost. Informed written consent will be taken from every patient before enrolment. Each and every patient will enjoy their rights to participate, refuse or withdraw from the study at any point of the study. Patients not willing to be a part of the study or not fulfilling the inclusion criteria will not be included. Patients who will deny to continue taking part in study will be treated as before. The investigator will also have the right to collect information about health condition, treatment and laboratory reports.

Expected Outcome:

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether Hangeoreum, a culturally tailored, self-paced, web-based program, is feasible and acceptable for Korean immigrants aged 50 and older who experience loneliness, and whether participants report improvements in loneliness and other aspects of psychosocial well-being after using the program. Hangeoreum is based on acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), which teaches practical skills to help people respond to difficult thoughts and feelings while taking meaningful actions guided by their personal values.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Can participants complete the Hangeoreum program as planned?
* Is the program feasible, acceptable, appropriate, and easy to use?
* Do participants show reductions in loneliness and improvements in social connectedness and other psychosocial outcomes after completing the program?
* What are participants' experiences with the program, and what suggestions do they have for improving it?

Participants will:

* Complete six self-paced weekly online modules over approximately 6-7 weeks.
* Complete online questionnaires before starting and after completing the program.
* Take part in one online interview about their experiences with the program.
primary_outcomes: Enrollment rate
Retention
Web-based module completion
title: Hangeoreum: A Self-Paced Web-Based Program for Loneliness and Connectedness Among Korean Immigrants Aged 50 and Older

brief_summary:
This study is for adults and adolescents who are at least 12 years old and have bronchiectasis. People can participate if they completed a previous study with the study medicine called verducatib. The purpose of this study is to find out how well verducatib is tolerated when people with bronchiectasis take it for a long time. The study also looks at breathing problems, how often lung flare-ups happen, and how quickly lung function changes.

This is a roll-over study for participants who completed a previous study with verducatib: AIRTIVITY® (1397-0014) or CLAIRLEAF® (1397-0017). All participants receive verducatib. Participants take verducatib as tablets once a day at home. They may continue their usual treatment for bronchiectasis during the study.

Participants can stay in the study for up to 1 year and 9 months. Treatment with verducatib can continue for up to 1 year and 6 months. About 6 study visits are done at the study site and about 4 are done by phone. At all visits, the doctors check participants' health and collect information on any health problems that occur during the study. The doctors also look at lung flare-ups and measure lung function over time.
primary_outcomes: Occurrence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) over the course of this trial
title: A Study to Learn How Well People With Bronchiectasis Tolerate Continued Treatment With Verducatib After Earlier Studies (AIRTIVITY®-ON)

brief_summary:
Coeliac disease is a lifelong autoimmune condition in which the immune system reacts to gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley and rye, affecting about 1% of the general population. The only currently approved treatment is a strict, lifelong gluten-free diet (GFD). Although strict adherence to a gluten-free diet leads to mucosal recovery in most patients, up to 20-30% of coeliac patients continue to experience persistent gastrointestinal symptoms (such as abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhoea or constipation). Furthermore, commercially prepared gluten-free products often contain higher amounts of fat, sugar and salt, and lower amounts of fibre, protein, folate and vitamins compared with gluten-containing equivalents.

Conversely, the Mediterranean diet-rich in vegetables, fruits, legumes, fish, nuts and extra-virgin olive oil-is widely recognised for its benefits on cardiovascular, metabolic and gut health, as well as quality of life, in contrast to diets rich in highly or ultra-processed foods.

This multicentre cross-sectional observational study aims to evaluate whether adult coeliac patients on a long-term strict gluten-free diet whose habitual diet more closely aligns with the Mediterranean dietary pattern are less likely to experience persistent gastrointestinal symptoms and have a better quality of life and nutritional status, and conversely whether higher consumption of highly processed foods is associated with worse symptoms, poorer quality of life and less adequate nutritional status. No dietary intervention is provided as part of the study; participants complete validated questionnaires and undergo routine anthropometric and blood assessments during a single regular outpatient follow-up visit.
primary_outcomes: Celiac Disease Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (CeD-GSRS) Score
Celiac Disease-Specific Quality of Life (CD-QOL) Score
Pyramid-based Mediterranean Diet Score (PyrMDS)
Body Mass Index (BMI)
title: Impact of Mediterranean Diet and Processed Food Consumption on Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Coeliac Patients on a Gluten-Free Diet

brief_summary:
This is a two-center, randomized, open-label, factorial controlled trial. This trial aims to evaluate the efficacy of exposure to sucrose and ice, alone and in combination, compared to control, in reducing oral pruritus during allergy procedures.

The population will include patients aged 8 years and older presenting with oral pruritus in the context of an oral food challenge or an oral immunotherapy dose increase at the allergy clinic.

Clinically significant oral pruritus will be defined as a pruritus intensity of ≥3/10 on the ICH NRS, and a symptom bothersome enough that the patient would normally seek treatment.

Eligible participants will be randomized to one of four groups (1:1:1:1 ratio):

* Sucrose only (3.5 g granulated sugar)
* Cold only (20 mL of ice in the form of popsicle)
* Sucrose + cold (20 mL frozen sucrose solution)
* Control (20 mL room-temperature water)

Participants will be asked to report when the pruritus has decreased to a level at which they would not normally seek treatment, as well as when it has completely resolved.

The evolution of oral pruritus will be assessed using an 11-point Numeric Rating Scale (ICH NRS). Pruritus intensity will be measured every 30 seconds during the first 5 minutes after administration of the study intervention and then every 1 minute until 15 minutes post-intervention.
primary_outcomes: Area under the curve (AUC) of ICH NRS scores
title: Evaluating Sucrose and Cold Oral Interventions for the Treatment of Oral Pruritus During Allergy Procedures.

brief_summary: Alteplase, a recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA), is commonly used for thrombolytic treatment in patients with high-risk acute pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE), whereas the role of thrombolysis in intermediate-risk PTE remains controversial. This multicenter, randomized controlled trial will compare the efficacy and safety of reduced-dose alteplase (25 mg administered intravenously over 2 hours) plus standard anticoagulation with standard anticoagulation alone in patients with intermediate-risk PTE who have high-risk features.
lead_sponsor: China National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases

brief_summary:
Some cancer treatments, such as anthracycline chemotherapy and HER2-targeted therapy, can damage the heart (cardiotoxicity). If heart damage is detected early, heart-protective treatment can be started and cancer treatment can often continue without interruption.

Heart ultrasound (echocardiography) is the standard method for monitoring the heart during cancer treatment. Today, heart function is mainly assessed with two-dimensional (2D) measurements, which may miss early changes. A newer technique, three-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (3D strain), follows the heart muscle's movement in all directions and may detect damage earlier and more accurately.

The SAFE HEART study will investigate whether 3D strain detects early heart damage better than 2D strain and conventional measures of pumping function (ejection fraction) in adults with breast cancer, lymphoma or sarcoma who are treated with anthracyclines and/or HER2-targeted therapy at Skåne University Hospital in Lund and Malmö, Sweden.

Participants undergo heart ultrasound, ECG and blood tests for cardiac biomarkers (troponin I and NT-proBNP) before, during and after cancer treatment. Blood samples are also stored in a biobank to search for new markers that can predict heart damage. Participants who develop signs of heart damage, and a matched group without heart damage, may be asked to undergo a cardiac magnetic resonance (MRI) scan.
conditions: Anthracycline Related Cardiotoxicity in Breast Cancer
primary_outcomes: Change in 3D left ventricular strain parameters compared with 2D global longitudinal strain during follow-up
title: 3D Versus 2D Strain Echocardiography for Early Detection of Cardiotoxicity During Cancer Therapy

brief_summary: This is a prospective, single-center, controlled real-world study in patients with advanced solid tumors (stage III-IV) receiving chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, or endocrine therapy. Participants who choose the digital management group use a smartphone-based oncology management application with medication reminders, AI-assisted laboratory report interpretation, adverse event self-reporting, and clinician alerts for critical values. Participants who choose the conventional group receive routine outpatient follow-up and telephone contact without digital tools. The study follows participants for 12 months to compare the incidence of overall and severe (CTCAE grade ≥3) adverse events, emergency department visits, 30-day readmission, dose reduction, treatment delay/missed doses, and time to adverse event recovery. The aim is to evaluate whether a digital whole-course management model improves medication safety, reduces healthcare burden, and supports treatment adherence in advanced cancer care.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of any-grade adverse events
Incidence of severe adverse events (CTCAE grade ≥3)
title: AI-Assisted Whole-Course Management for Medication Safety and Healthcare Burden in Advanced Solid Tumors: A Prospective Controlled Study

brief_summary:
Cerebral palsy (CP) is the leading cause of neurological disability in children, with a prevalence of 2-2.5 per 1,000 live births in Europe. It results from irreversible injury to the developing brain and is characterized by permanent disorders of movement and posture, frequently associated with cognitive or sensory impairments. Although the primary lesion is non-progressive, secondary musculoskeletal complications evolve over time, leading to soft tissue contractures and skeletal deformities. Hemiplegia, the most common CP subtype (≈30%), predominantly affects the upper limb, where spasticity and dyskinesia impair both unimanual and bimanual function.

Focal management with botulinum toxin combined with task-oriented therapy has demonstrated functional benefits. However, evidence supporting orthopedic interventions for contractures and deformities remains limited, and functional outcomes following upper limb surgery in CP are insufficiently documented. Selective and hyperselective peripheral neurotomies are established treatments for focal spasticity in adults, yet their role in paediatric CP remains debated.

To date, no study has systematically compared unilateral and bilateral selective or hyperselective upper limb neurotomies in children with CP, nor analysed medium- and long-term functional trajectories within a structured multidisciplinary decision-making framework. The investigators report the outcomes of a paediatric cohort managed through a standardized pathway including multidimensional preoperative assessment, shared decision-making in a multidisciplinary meeting, specialized neurosurgical intervention, and protocolized postoperative rehabilitation and orthotic management. Functional impact is assessed at discharge and at 6 and 12-15 months.

This study aims to provide original comparative data on the magnitude and durability of functional gains in unimanual and bimanual performance, identify potential responder profiles, and clarify the position of neurotomy within the therapeutic algorithm for the spastic upper limb in children with CP. Ultimately, the findings may contribute to refining indication criteria, optimizing surgical timing, and improving participation and autonomy outcomes.
interventions: Peripheral neurotomy of the upper limb (musculocutaneous and/or median and/or ulnar).
primary_outcomes: Melbourne Test - Version 2 (MA2).
title: Peripheral Neurotomies of the Upper Limb in Children With Cerebral Palsy.

This study aimed to evaluate the effect of parasternal and rectointercostal block administration-performed to achieve pain control and reduce the postoperative analgesic burden-on patient postoperative recovery and extubation time."

brief_summary:
The purpose of this randomized controlled trial is to compare the outcomes of two laparoscopic techniques for repairing inguinal hernia in children: laparoscopic percutaneous extraperitoneal closure (LPEC) and laparoscopic intracorporeal suture (LIS). The study will be conducted in the Department of Pediatric Surgery, Bahawal Victoria Hospital, Bahawalpur, and will enroll children aged 1 to 15 years of either gender who have a unilateral or bilateral inguinal hernia and are planned for laparoscopic repair. Children with recurrent, incarcerated, or previously operated hernias, coagulopathy, undescended testes, major congenital abdominal anomalies, congenital heart disease, or cerebral palsy will be excluded.

Participants will be randomly assigned, using sealed opaque envelopes, to one of two groups. Group A will undergo LPEC, in which the hernia sac is closed extraperitoneally with a needle passed percutaneously around the internal inguinal ring under laparoscopic view. Group B will undergo LIS, in which sutures are placed and tied entirely within the abdominal cavity. All operations will be performed by a single surgical team trained in both techniques.

The main outcome is hernia recurrence at 3 months. Secondary outcomes are operating time, post-operative pain (FLACC score at 12 hours, assessed by a resident blinded to the technique), hospital stay, wound infection within 30 days, other intra- and post-operative complications, and time to return to full activity. Children will be followed weekly in the outpatient clinic and assessed for recurrence at 3 months.

The study hypothesizes that recurrence at 3 months is higher with the intraperitoneal (LIS) approach than with the extraperitoneal (LPEC) approach.
primary_outcomes: Hernia recurrence
title: Comparing Two Laparoscopic Techniques for Hernia Repair in Children

brief_summary: Current eating disorder (ED) treatment options are both inaccessible (80% of people with EDs do not access treatment) and not entirely successful (most people with an ED do not reach full remission). Imaginal exposure therapy, or what the investigators call Be Body Brave (BBB), is self-guided treatment that offers a solution to both of these issues: online modules reduce barriers to access treatment, and exposure therapy has the potential to shift cognitive beliefs in eating disorders, creating lasting change. This study aims to determine the effectiveness of BBB and identify the optimal timing for implementation of exposure therapy for eating disorders. Participants will complete five sessions of digital imaginal exposure and complete posttreatment, 1-month, 6-month, and 12-month follow-up questionnaires assessing eating disorder symptoms, quality of life, and clinical impairment.
primary_outcomes: Eating disorder behaviors
Fear of weight gain
Body image disturbance (State Body Disturbances)
Food avoidance
Fear of food
Eating disorder fears
title: Be Body Brave: Digital Written Exposure Therapy for Eating Disorders
