brief_summary:
This study will examine whether computer-assisted vocabulary instruction in Spanish and English helps young bilingual children with developmental language disorder learn and use vocabulary. It will include 120 Spanish-English bilingual children in kindergarten or first grade. Eighty children with developmental language disorder will be assigned by chance to bilingual computer-assisted vocabulary instruction, English-only computer-assisted vocabulary instruction, or usual English-language school services. Forty children with typical language development will receive bilingual instruction without random assignment, providing a developmental comparison.

The program teaches 36 vocabulary concepts through 24 small-group sessions, ordinarily over about six weeks. School-calendar disruptions may extend the schedule. Vocabulary will be assessed in both languages before intervention, immediately afterward, and approximately six weeks after the final session. The primary outcomes are naming and defining the taught concepts in each language.

The implementation component anticipates 15 unique school speech-language pathologists or appropriately supervised speech-language pathology assistants across five project years, with a planning target of approximately 3 new clinicians per year. Annual recruitment may vary with eligible caseloads. This component examines delivery fidelity, feasibility, clinician confidence, usability and satisfaction. Teacher and parent feedback about children's vocabulary use, communication confidence and engagement will also be collected after intervention and at follow-up where feasible.
primary_outcomes: Target vocabulary Naming in Spanish
Target vocabulary Definition in Spanish
Target vocabulary Naming in English
Target vocabulary Definition in English
title: Computer-Assisted Vocabulary Intervention for Spanish-English Bilingual Children With Developmental Language Disorder

brief_summary:
Purpose: This study aims to evaluate the effect of the 4-7-8 breathing technique applied before central venous catheter (CVC) insertion on patients' anxiety, pain, and vital signs.

Design: A single-center, randomized controlled experimental study. Methods: The study plans to recruit adult patients undergoing CVC insertion. Participants will be randomly allocated to either the 4-7-8 breathing intervention group or the standard-care control group. The intervention group will perform the 4-7-8 breathing technique before the CVC insertion procedure, whereas the control group will receive routine standard care. Data will be collected using a participant information form, State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain, and a vital signs follow-up form. Statistical analyses will include independent-samples and paired-samples t-tests, the Mann-Whitney U test, and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test to compare the groups
primary_outcomes: State Anxiety Level
Pain
title: Effect of the 4-7-8 Breathing Technique Before Central Venous Catheter Insertion

brief_summary:

Study objective - to investigate the efficacy and safety of levosimendan in patients in the perioperative period following pulmonary endarterectomy for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH).

brief_summary:
Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is a major cause of morbidity in hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients, with both direct effects, including CMV disease, and indirect effects, such as graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) and increased immunosuppression.

Virological monitoring and preemptive treatment with ganciclovir have reduced the incidence of CMV disease from approximately 30% to 2-6%, but have not eliminated the indirect morbidity associated with viral replication. Letermovir, a non-hematotoxic antiviral agent targeting the CMV terminase complex, has demonstrated efficacy in preventing CMV infection in this population.

The CIRCLE study aims to describe the evolution of global and CMV-specific immune reconstitution in CMV-seropositive hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients receiving or not receiving letermovir prophylaxis, and to characterize the immune response over time.
primary_outcomes: Viral load of torque teno virus (TTV) in whole blood
Qualitative and functional assessment of natural killer (NK) cells
CMV-specific cellular immune response
CMV-specific IgG concentration in plasma
Time to development of a significant CMV-specific cellular immune response
Number of participants with CMV infection
Number of participants with CMV disease
title: Specific Immune Reconstitution After Allogeneic Transplantation and Letermovir Prophylaxis

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to develop and evaluate an intelligent system based on generative artificial intelligence (AI) for assessing clinical thinking and decision-making abilities in medical students.

The study will examine whether the AI-based evaluation system can provide reliable and valid assessments of medical students' performance in clinical scenarios. Participants will complete clinical case-based tasks designed to assess their clinical reasoning and decision-making abilities. Their responses will be evaluated using the AI-based system and compared with assessments made using established evaluation methods and/or expert ratings.

The findings of this study may help determine whether generative AI can be used as a practical tool for assessing clinical thinking and decision-making skills in medical education.
primary_outcomes: Change in Clinical Reasoning Score on Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE)
title: Generative AI-Based Evaluation of Clinical Thinking and Decision-Making in Medical Students

brief_summary:
Patients with locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) may receive chemotherapy combined with immunotherapy before surgery to reduce tumor size. However, some patients do not respond adequately to this initial treatment, and additional treatment options are needed.

This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of combining becotatug vedotin (MRG003), an antibody-drug conjugate that targets the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), with pucotenlimab (HX008), a PD-1 immune checkpoint inhibitor, in patients whose disease remains stable or progresses after induction immunotherapy combined with platinum-based chemotherapy.

This is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm, phase II clinical trial. Eligible patients with locally advanced, resectable HNSCC will receive two cycles of becotatug vedotin plus pucotenlimab, administered every three weeks before surgery. After treatment, patients will undergo tumor response assessment followed by curative-intent surgery and appropriate postoperative treatment.

The primary objective is to evaluate the objective response rate (ORR), defined as the proportion of patients achieving complete or partial tumor response. The study will also assess pathological response, surgical outcomes, treatment safety, and long-term survival.

The study seeks to determine whether this additional preoperative treatment strategy may improve tumor response and provide further opportunities for organ preservation in patients who have not benefited adequately from initial induction immunochemotherapy.
conditions: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Head and Neck (SCCHN)
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR)
title: Becotatug Vedotin Plus Pucotenlimab in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma With Suboptimal Response to Induction Immunochemotherapy

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a bioceramic root canal medicament reduces bacteria better than calcium hydroxide in adults with asymptomatic apical periodontitis (a long-standing infection at the tip of the tooth root that does not cause pain) in upper front teeth.

The main question it aims to answer is:

Does the bioceramic medicament (Bio-C Temp) lower the amount of bacteria in the end portion (apical third) of the root canal more than calcium hydroxide (UltraCal XS)?

Researchers will compare the bioceramic medicament with calcium hydroxide to see which one leaves fewer bacteria in the root canal after 14 days.

Participants will:

Receive standard root canal cleaning and shaping on one upper front tooth Have bacterial samples taken from the root canal before and after cleaning Be randomly assigned to receive either the bioceramic or the calcium hydroxide medicament inside the root canal for 14 days Return after 14 days for a final bacterial sample before the root canal treatment is continued

The amount of bacteria in each sample will be measured in the laboratory using quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR).
primary_outcomes: Bacterial Load in the Apical Third of the Root Canal
title: Bacterial Reduction in Apical Root Canals After Bioceramic or Calcium Hydroxide Medicament

brief_summary: This phase II trial tests how well enzomenib works in treating patients with prostate cancer that has spread from where it first started (primary site) to other places in the body (metastatic) and has continued to grow or spread despite androgen deprivation therapy (castration-resistant). The growth and survival of prostate tumor cells often depends on testosterone. Androgen deprivation therapy blocks the use of testosterone by the tumor cells. Although most tumors respond to androgen deprivation therapy at first, nearly all eventually progress to a castration-resistant state. Enzomenib, a menin inhibitor, targets and blocks menin, a protein that plays a role in the survival and growth of tumor cells.
conditions: Stage IVB Prostate Cancer AJCC v8

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether ketamine given for procedural analgesia changes intracranial pressure in adult emergency department patients. Intracranial pressure is assessed non-invasively by measuring optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) with bedside ultrasonography. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does ONSD change after ketamine administration compared with the measurement taken before ketamine?
* Does the change in ONSD differ between patients receiving 0.5 mg/kg and 1 mg/kg ketamine? Participants who receive intravenous ketamine as part of their routine emergency care will have ONSD, vital signs, and pain scores recorded before ketamine administration and at 2, 5, 15, and 30 minutes after administration.
primary_outcomes: Change in Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter From Baseline

brief_summary:
Hormonal contraceptives are widely used by women to prevent pregnancy. However, some women experience sexual problems, such as reduced sexual desire, difficulty becoming sexually aroused, inadequate lubrication, difficulty reaching orgasm, or pain during sexual activity. These problems may negatively affect women's psychological well-being and quality of life.

This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate whether counseling based on the PLISSIT model could improve sexual function and reduce psychological distress among women experiencing sexual dysfunction while using hormonal contraceptives.

A total of 374 eligible women were randomly assigned to two groups. The intervention group received structured counseling based on the PLISSIT model, which includes four levels: Permission, Limited Information, Specific Suggestions, and Intensive Therapy. The counseling was delivered through five interactive group sessions. The control group received routine care without the structured PLISSIT counseling intervention.

Sexual function was assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), while psychological distress was assessed using the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K10). Both outcomes were measured before the intervention and four weeks after the intervention.

The study sought to determine whether PLISSIT-based counseling could improve women's sexual function and reduce psychological distress compared with routine care. The findings may help inform the development of nursing counseling interventions that address women's sexual health and psychological well-being.
primary_outcomes: Change in Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) Total Score
title: PLISSIT Model Counseling on Sexual Function and Psychological Distress Among Hormonal Contraceptive Users

brief_summary:
The main purpose of this study is to understand how safe and well-tolerated LY4247147 is in participants with obesity or overweight who are otherwise healthy. Blood tests will be performed to check how much LY4247147 gets into the bloodstream and how long it takes the body to eliminate it.

The study will be conducted in 3 parts. For each participant in Parts A and C, the study will last about 30 weeks and will include a stay in the Clinical Research Unit (CRU) lasting about 8 nights. brief_summary: This research was conducted as a randomized controlled experimental study to examine the effect of music listening during drain removal on pain in patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty. The study was carried out between March 19, 2024, and October 15, 2025, in the orthopedics and traumatology clinic of a state hospital in Türkiye. The sample consisted of 60 adult patients. Patients were randomly divided into intervention and control groups. Patients in the intervention group were played the Acemaşiran Maqam of Turkish Classical MP3 music, prepared by the group of Turkish Music Research and Promotion (TÜMATA) in Türkiye, via headphones for a total of 30 minutes, starting 15 minutes before and continuing for 15 minutes after drain removal. Patients in the control group received no intervention. Before the drain removal procedure, the "Patient Demographic Characteristic Form" including the sociodemographic characteristics of the patients and the VAS pain scale were completed by the researcher through face-to-face interviews. Pain levels of patients were re-evaluated using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) pain scale immediately after, and 15 minutes after drain removal. The study expected that patients in the intervention group will have more favorable pain scores compared to the control group. brief_summary:
Transcutaneous hypoglossal nerve stimulation is an emerging treatment option for Obstructive Sleep Apnoea (OSA), a sleep condition where breathing is repeatedly limited. The standard treatment for OSA is not always well tolerated therefore, more alternatives are needed.

Transcutaneous hypoglossal nerve stimulation uses a device, such as Zeus, which sticks underneath the chin to deliver electrical pulses during sleep. These pulses stimulate the hypoglossal nerve to prevent the tongue from relaxing and blocking the airway.

Device placement is important for specific nerve targeting; however, its proximity is close to receptors involved in blood pressure regulation. Whilst current research indicates that transcutaneous stimulation is unlikely to increase blood pressure, OSA patients have an increased risk of developing high blood pressure, therefore treatment options should not make this worse. Further research to understand the impact of transcutaneous hypoglossal nerve stimulation on blood pressure is therefore needed. In this study, the blood pressure of participants will be measured whilst they wear the Zeus sleep device. It is expected that blood pressure will either decrease or remain constant in line with current research. Findings could facilitate improved confidence in device use for OSA treatment and provide patients with alternative treatment options.

This study overcomes these barriers by transitioning survivors to community adult primary care providers (PCPs) after orienting PCPs to survivors' individual survivorship care needs and educating YA CCS regarding health self-management/advocacy. This study includes a remote transition approach for YA survivorship care that leverages community PCPs, telehealth, and nurse navigators (NNs). BRIDGES-YAS! will investigate a novel, remote, multi-level intervention to transition YA CCS to community adult PCPs for a survivorship visit versus usual cancer treatment center (CTC) based follow-up care (plus educational handout about transition). The 1-year intervention includes: 1) tailored telehealth CCS education and resource navigation with self-management and self-advocacy skills training by a CTC NN, 2) brief, structured, interactive phone handoff by CTC NN to the community PCP conveying the CCS's individualized survivorship care needs, 3) secure electronic storage on CCS' smartphone (or other device) of Survivorship Care Plan and established health education materials, and 4) ongoing NN support and communication between CCS, CTC, and PCP. If successful, this intervention strategy could readily be deployed in cancer treatment centers to improve adult survivor access to quality, community-based survivorship care.

The primary aim of this study is to compare the frequency and severity of overactive bladder (OAB) symptoms and urinary incontinence (UI) in women diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) with a control group of healthy women. Secondary aims are to examine the relationships between the presence of OAB symptoms and UI in RA patients and demographic characteristics, disease duration, and disease activity; and to evaluate the impact of these symptoms on the quality of life of RA patients and healthy controls.

This multicenter, cross-sectional study will include women diagnosed with RA and healthy women of similar age. The sample size was calculated using G\*Power 3.1 software with 80% power and a 5% alpha margin of error, assuming a prevalence of lower urinary tract symptoms of 60% in the RA group and 40% in the control group. A minimum of 95 participants/group was determined to detect a 20% difference between the two groups. Subgroup analyses were planned to include a total of 900 participants, with 450 participants from each group, to balance inter-center heterogeneity and compensate for potential data loss. Data collection tools included demographic information (age, body mass index, menopausal status, smoking and alcohol use, education level, occupation, and number of births), disease duration in the RA group, and disease activity (DAS-28). The Overactive Bladder Symptom Score (OABSS), the International Incontinence Counseling Questionnaire - Short Form (ICIQ-SF), and the Incontinence Impact Questionnaire (IIQ-7) scales were used to assess OAB symptoms (frequent urination, nocturia, urge incontinence) and quality of life with UI. Dependent variables were OAB symptoms (frequent urination, nocturia, urge incontinence) and quality of life, while independent variables were demographic characteristics, RA disease duration, DAS-28, and the group variable. Data will be analyzed using SPSS software; in addition to descriptive statistics, independent samples t-test or Mann-Whitney U test, Chi-square test, correlation analyses, and logistic regression for AAM symptoms will be applied according to the appropriate distribution. The significance level will be accepted as p\<0.05.

brief_summary:
Background:

Early initiation of breastfeeding is critical for neonatal health, survival, and cognitive development. However, global rates of early initiation and exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) remain suboptimal, particularly in low-resource settings. Common barriers include improper positioning, poor attachment, delayed milk flow, and cultural practices such as prelacteal feeding. Oketani breast massage-a Japanese technique involving soft massage on breast is a low-cost, non-invasive method believed to improve milk flow and relieve early breastfeeding difficulties. This study aimed to examine whether integrating Oketani breast massage with standard breastfeeding counseling enhances early initiation of breastmilk flow of mothers in Bangladesh.

Methods:

The investigators conducted a randomized controlled trial across 12 health facilities in Bangladesh, enrolling 630 healthy mothers with full term singleton babies. Participants were randomized equally to one of the three groups: (1) routine care (control), (2) breastfeeding counseling with positioning and attachment, or (3) Breastfeeding counseling plus Oketani breast massage. Primary outcomes included number of feeds in the first 24 hours, total suckling episodes in the first 3 days, and time to establish continuous flow of breastmilk. Secondary outcomes included early initiation of breastfeeding, colostrum feeding, maternal comfort, and breastfeeding problems. Data were analyzed using t-test, ANOVA, chi-square tests, and intention-to-treat principles.

Results:

Baseline characteristics were comparable among all groups. Mothers in the counseling plus Oketani group breastfed more frequently than the control mothers in the first 24 hours (10.6 ± 2.3 vs. 8.9 ± 2.9; p \< 0.001), had more total suckling episodes in 3 days (43.2 ± 4.8 vs. 29.1 ± 4.8; p \< 0.001), and achieved continuous milk flow sooner (1.9 ± 0.5 vs. 4.3 ± 2.5 days; p \< 0.001). Rates of early initiation (91.0% vs. 36.7%), colostrum feeding (91.0% vs. 36.7%), and hygienic practices were significantly higher in intervention groups than the control mothers. Mothers receiving Oketani massage expressed improved confidence, softer breasts, and fewer feeding difficulties.

Mothers in the counselling plus Oketani group breastfed more frequently within the first 24 hours and achieved continuous milk flow significantly earlier than those in the counselling-only group. Although total sucking during the first 3 days was slightly higher in the Oketani group, the difference was not statistically significant. Overall, these findings suggest that Oketani massage provided additional benefit in improving early breastfeeding frequency and accelerating milk flow establishment.

Conclusion:

Enhanced counseling with Oketani breast massage significantly enhanced early initiation of breastfeeding (EIB) practices and breast milk flow with higher frequency of breastfeeding and maternal comfort compared to routine Breastfeeding practices. These low-cost interventions can enhance breastfeeding in the postnatal care to strengthen exclusive breastfeeding and reduce the risk of feeding breastmilk substitutes.
interventions: Oketani Breast Massage and Breastfeeding Counseling
primary_outcomes: Number of Breastfeeding Sessions in the First 24 Hours Postpartum
Total Suckling Episodes in the First 3 Days
Time to Establish Continuous Breastmilk Flow
title: Oketani Massage Enhances Postpartum Early Breastfeeding Flow

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial will investigate the immediate effects of virtual reality (VR) exergaming on reaction time, physical performance, balance, and muscle activity in children aged 10-14 years with different athletic backgrounds.

The study aims to enroll 360 children divided into three categories: 120 rhythmic gymnasts, 120 athletes participating in other competitive sports, and 120 children who do not regularly participate in organized sports. Within each category, participants will be randomly assigned to either a VR exergaming group or an active control group performing comparable physical movements without VR.

Each participant will attend one testing session. Before and after the assigned three-minute activity, children will complete three assessments: a computerized reaction time test, a Five Times Sit-to-Stand test, and a single-leg balance test. Small, noninvasive sensors placed on the arms and legs will record muscle electrical activity and movement characteristics during selected activities.

The primary objective is to determine whether VR exergaming produces different immediate changes in reaction time compared with similar physical activity performed without VR. Secondary objectives include evaluating changes in functional performance and postural control, examining muscle activation patterns, and investigating whether responses to VR differ according to athletic background.

The findings may improve understanding of the immediate cognitive-motor and neuromuscular responses to immersive VR activities in children.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Median Choice Reaction Time (Milliseconds)
title: Effects of Virtual Reality Exergaming on Reaction Time, Physical Performance, and Muscle Activity in Children

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the safety, visual performance, and potential clinical benefits of the LENTIS® MAX LS-313 MF80 intraocular lens compared with the monofocal LENTIS® L-313 intraocular lens in adult patients with cataract in both eyes and clinically stable or inactive late age-related macular degeneration.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Is corrected distance vision with the LENTIS® MAX LS-313 MF80 not worse than corrected distance vision with the monofocal LENTIS® L-313? Is distance-corrected near vision with the LENTIS® MAX LS-313 MF80 not worse than, and potentially better than, near vision with the monofocal LENTIS® L-313?
2. Researchers will compare the two lenses within the same participant: each participant will receive the LENTIS® MAX LS-313 MF80 in one eye and the monofocal LENTIS® L-313 in the other eye. This will allow researchers to compare distance and near vision between the two eyes.

Participants will:

* undergo cataract surgery in both eyes, with implantation of the LENTIS® MAX LS-313 MF80 in one eye and the LENTIS® L-313 in the other eye;
* attend postoperative follow-up visits, including the main assessment at 4-6 months and a longer-term assessment at 11-14 months after the first-eye surgery;
* undergo eye examinations and vision testing, including distance and near visual acuity, refraction, eye-pressure measurements, retinal imaging, visual-field testing, and other ophthalmic examinations; and
* complete study-specific assessments of vision-related quality of life and activities of daily living and perform a home-based visual training programme following implantation of the LENTIS® MAX LS-313 MF80.
primary_outcomes: Monocular Corrected Distance Visual Acuity (CDVA) at 4 m
Monocular Distance-Corrected Near Visual Acuity (DCNVA) at preferred reading distance
title: Safety and Clinical Performance of the LENTIS® MAX LS-313 MF80 Compared With the Monofocal L-313 in Cataract Patients With Late Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Multicenter Comparative Clinical Investigation.

Then comparison will be made in terms of length of hospital stay in days and time for ambulation in hours. Results will be compared showing which protocol is better and cost effective.

brief_summary: This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of a 16-week course of low-dose naltrexone (LDN) in approximately 1,300 participants aged 6 to 25 years with fatigue associated with Long COVID. Participants will be enrolled across three age cohorts (6-11, 12-17, and 18-25 years) and randomized 1:1 to receive LDN capsules or matching placebo capsules. LDN will be initiated at 1.5 mg daily and titrated weekly to a maximum tolerated dose of up to 4.5 mg daily. Randomization will be stratified by age cohort, and participants will also be randomized to a pharmacokinetic (PK) sampling window. Primary objective is to compare the change in fatigue severity from baseline to 16 weeks between participants aged 6 to 25 years with Long COVID randomized to a 16-week course of LDN or placebo.
lead_sponsor: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in Pediatric Quality of Life - Multidimensional Fatigue Scale (PedsQL-MFS) total score.
title: The Study of Brave-LC LDN Treatment Trial

brief_summary:
Lever positioning manipulation (LPM) is used to treat pain associated with lumbar disc herniation (LDH), but treatment-associated changes in cortical functional organization remain unclear. This prospective nonrandomized study will examine cortical surface-based resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) measures before and after a 4-week course of LPM.

The target is 30 participants with LDH completing treatment-period assessments and 30 age- and sex-matched healthy controls completing baseline assessment. Participants who withdraw will be replaced as needed, and all enrolled and replacement participants will be counted. Participants with LDH will receive LPM three times weekly for 4 weeks, approximately 20 minutes per session. MRI and clinical scales will be collected before treatment and at week 4 after the first session. Healthy controls will undergo baseline MRI only and receive no intervention. The eight primary imaging outcome groups cover amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF), regional homogeneity (ReHo), global functional connectivity density, seed-to-vertex connectivity, region-to-region connectivity, within- and between-network connectivity, functional connectivity gradients, and gradient eccentricity. Clinical outcomes include VAS, JOA, ODI, SAS and SDS scores. Adverse events will be monitored throughout treatment.
lead_sponsor: The Third Affiliated hospital of Zhejiang Chinese Medical University
primary_outcomes: Change in Cortical Surface-Based Mean-Normalized Amplitude of Low-Frequency Fluctuations
Change in Cortical Surface-Based Regional Homogeneity
Change in Cortical Surface-Based Global Functional Connectivity Density
Change in Cortical Surface-Based Seed-to-Vertex Functional Connectivity
Change in Cortical Region-to-Region Functional Connectivity
Change in Within-Network and Between-Network Cortical Functional Connectivity
Change in Cortical Functional Connectivity Gradient Scores
Change in Cortical Functional Gradient Eccentricity
title: Cortical Surface Functional Changes After Lever Positioning Manipulation for Lumbar Disc Herniation

brief_summary:
The main objective of this study is to determine whether an 8-week inspiratory muscle training (IMT) programme, delivered at home through telerehabilitation, improves ventilatory efficiency (VE/VCO2 slope) compared with a sham (placebo) training programme in adults with pulmonary hypertension. Secondary objectives are to analyse its effects on airway inflammation, inspiratory muscle strength, lung function, ventilatory pattern and mechanical efficiency during exercise, dyspnoea and health-related quality of life.

Forty participants will be randomly allocated (1:1) to active IMT or sham IMT. Both groups will train twice a day, 5 days a week, for 8 weeks, with biweekly load adjustments and supervision through video calls. Participants, therapists, outcome assessors and the statistician will be blinded to group allocation.
primary_outcomes: Ventilatory efficiency (VE/VCO2 slope)
title: Home-based Inspiratory Muscle Training in Pulmonary Hypertension

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to assess the acceptance and usability as well as safety of the AutoSTEA device is in treating epigastric pain syndrome in adults. It will also explore preliminary clinical and mechanistic signals. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the AutoSTEA device ease epigastric pain symptoms?
* Is the AutoSTEA device safe and feasible for patients to use at their home?

Participants will:

* Use the device for 30-60 minutes at home each day for 4 weeks
* Have a phone check-in four times through the trial (once a week).
* Answer the daily and weekly questionnaires which consist of questions regarding symptoms, device usability, and adverse events experienced.

Patient's Operating Experience with the Device when Self-Administered at Home as Assessed by the Weekly Safety and Adverse Events Questionnaire
title: TEA Synchronized With Natural Breathing for EPS

brief_summary:
Most cases of Infective endocarditis (IE) are caused by Gram-positive bacteria, primarily Staphylococcus aureus, oral or intestinal streptococci, and enterococci (especially Enterococcus faecalis). Blood cultures for these bacteria may indicate simple bacteremia (without cardiac involvement) or endocarditis. The proportion of patients with IE among those presenting with positive blood cultures varies depending on the pathogen (approximately 10% for S. aureus, 5 to 50% for oral streptococci, depending on the species, and 15% for E. faecalis).

The PPSIE study aims to identify a specific biological signature of infective endocarditis that would allow identification of valvular involvement in patients with positive blood cultures.

Patients will be selected based on a blood culture positive for one of the following organisms: S. aureus, S. mutans, S. gordonii, S. sanguinis, S. parasanguinis, S. gallolyticus, S. mitis/oralis, E. faecalis, as well as based on the likelihood of endocarditis determined by a clinical score specific to the causative pathogen (VIRSTA, HANDOC, or DENOVA) A blood sample will be collected 1 day, 5 days, and 3 months after enrollment. Patients will be classified into the groups "bacteremia without cardiac involvement (BasAC)," "definite infectious endocarditis (confirmed IE)," or "possible infectious endocarditis" according to the Duke classification modified by the ISCVID in 2023; uncertain cases will be assessed by an adjudication committee. Untergeted metabolomic analysis will be performed on these blood samples in order to find a metabolic signature able to discriminate patients with endocarditis from those without cardiac involvement. The prediction model will be built using a total of 80 patients, comprising 40 "confirmed IE" patients and 40 "IE excluded" (BasAC) patients.

The model will then be validated using a randomly selected sample from the "possible IE" group, according to the Duke classification modified by the ISCVID in 2023.
primary_outcomes: Metabolomic signature
title: Metabolic Profiling Among Patients Suspected of Infective Endocarditis - PPSIE Comparing Metabolomes of Bloodstream Infections Versus Infective Endocarditis

brief_summary: A prospective, multicenter, open-label, phase II trial of PET/CT-guided maintenance therapy in newly diagnosed marginal zone lymphoma. After first-line immunochemotherapy, dual-tracer PET/CT (18F-FDG and 68Ga-Pentixafor) is performed. Patients with Deauville score 4-5 receive orelabrutinib 150 mg daily for 1 year; those with score 1-3 are observed. Primary endpoint: 2-year progression-free survival rate.
lead_sponsor: Cancer Institute and Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences
primary_outcomes: 24-month progression-free survival rate
title: PET/CT-Guided Maintenance Therapy in Previously Untreated MZL

brief_summary:
Aqualung Therapeutics Corporation has developed ALT-100, a humanized murine monoclonal antibody (mAb) that specifically targets and neutralizes extracellular nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (eNAMPT) and prevents activation of a dysregulated proinflammatory signaling cascade.

Pre-clinical and clinical information from acute respiratory distress syndrome and prostate cancer studies show a novel treatment option for the patients with androgen pathway modulator-resistant (APMR) prostate cancer and bone metastases. Secreted eNAMPT drives prostate cancer progression, and a humanized eNAMPT-neutralizing antibody prevented aggressive disease in preclinical models by Sun et al. The anti-fibrotic activity of the eNAMPT-neutralizing antibody acts on type I collagen turnover-the same biology as osteoblastic bone metastasis.

Bone-predominant androgen pathway modulator-resistant (APMR) prostate cancer is a common clinical problem. Treatment options are often limited after progression on ADT and androgen receptor pathway inhibitors. The bone microenvironment itself is still largely untargeted. No eNAMPT-directed therapy has been tested in any oncology population, and no trial has asked whether eNAMPT/toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) blockade can modify the osseous tumor microenvironment in humans. This trial would test a first-in-class agent aimed at the bone microenvironment rather than at the tumor alone, in a setting where most available therapies offer short-lived benefit.

This study will evaluate the safety, tolerability and efficacy of the use of ALT-100 for treatment of bone-predominant metastatic androgen pathway modulation resistant prostate cancer. The recommended phase 2 dose of ALT-100 for treatment of bone-predominant metastatic androgen pathway modulation resistant prostate cancer will also be determined in the phase 1 portion of this study.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of dose limiting toxicities
Percentage of participants who achieve a PSA decrease of at least 30%
Percentage of participants who achieve a PSA decrease of at least 50%
Radiographic progression-free survival
title: ALT-100 Monoclonal Antibody (mAb) in Bone-Predominant Metastatic Androgen Pathway Modulation Resistant (APMR) Prostate Cancer -- The ALTAR-100 Trial

brief_summary:
Knee osteoarthritis is a common joint condition that causes knee pain, stiffness, muscle weakness, and difficulty performing daily activities such as walking, climbing stairs, and standing up from a chair. Exercise therapy is commonly used to improve muscle strength, reduce pain, and restore physical function. However, some patients may find traditional strengthening exercises difficult because of pain and increased stress on the knee joint.

Blood flow restriction (BFR) training is a rehabilitation technique that uses a specialized cuff placed around the upper thigh to partially restrict blood flow during exercise. This technique may help improve muscle strength while using lighter exercise loads.

The purpose of this study is to investigate whether adding blood flow restriction training to traditional physical therapy and closed kinetic chain exercises provides additional benefits for patients with knee osteoarthritis.

This randomized controlled trial will include 60 male and female participants aged 40 to 60 years with mild to moderate knee osteoarthritis. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups, with 30 participants in each group.

The first group will receive traditional physical therapy exercises combined with closed kinetic chain exercises, such as mini-squats, step-ups, step-downs, partial lunges, and wall slides.

The second group will receive the same exercise program with the addition of blood flow restriction training.

Both groups will participate in supervised treatment sessions twice weekly for eight weeks, for a total of 16 sessions.

The researchers will assess knee pain, knee range of motion, quadriceps muscle strength, knee function, mobility and fall risk, quality of life, and patient satisfaction. Assessments will be conducted before treatment, immediately after the eight-week intervention, and one month after completing treatment.

The study aims to determine whether adding blood flow restriction training to closed kinetic chain exercises can improve rehabilitation outcomes in individuals with knee osteoarthritis.
interventions: Traditional and Closed Kinetic Chain Exercise Program
lead_sponsor: Rasha Abdel Kader Abdel Azeem Khtab
primary_outcomes: Change in Knee Pain Intensity Measured by the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS)
Change in Knee Range of Motion Measured by a Smartphone Digital Inclinometer
Change in Quadriceps Muscle Strength Measured by a Hand-Held Dynamometer
title: EFFECT OF ADDING BLOOD FLOW RESTRICTION TRAINING TO CLOSED CHAIN EXERCISE IN KNEE OSTEOARTHRITIS

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to find out whether a special type of magnetic resonance imaging ( MRI), called blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) MRI, can help measure how much oxygen is present in liver tumors. Tumors with low oxygen levels are described as being hypoxic.

Yttrium-90 (Y-90) is a type of radioactive material used to treat liver tumors, including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), a type of liver cancer. Y-90 is a form of radiation treatment delivered directly to liver tumors through tiny beads carried by blood vessels. These beads release radiation that damages and kills cancer cells while helping limit radiation exposure to surrounding healthy tissue. This treatment is also called Y-90 radioembolization or selective internal radiation therapy (SIRT).
interventions: Blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) magnetic resonance imaging ( MRI)
primary_outcomes: The number of successful novel blood oxygen level dependent (BOLD) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
title: Characterizing Tumor Hypoxia With BOLD-MRI to Predict Y-90 Treatment Response

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the effects of two different exercise programs, Pilates and combined resistance and aerobic training, on physical activity, kinesiophobia, quality of life, and disease-related outcomes in adults with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do the two exercise programs improve physical activity levels, reduce kinesiophobia, and improve quality of life in adults with IBD?
* Are there differences between Pilates and combined resistance and aerobic training in their effects on participants' health status and disease-related outcomes?

Researchers will compare participants assigned to the Pilates group and the combined resistance and aerobic training group with participants in the control group to evaluate the effects of the exercise programs.

Participants will be randomly allocated to one of three groups: a Pilates group, a combined resistance and aerobic training group, or a control group. Participants in the exercise groups will follow their assigned exercise program using online instructional videos twice a week for 12 weeks, with each session lasting 20-30 minutes. They will record completed exercise sessions in an exercise diary. All participants will complete questionnaires before and after the intervention to assess physical activity, kinesiophobia, quality of life, depressive symptoms, knowledge of physical activity, and attitudes towards physiotherapists. Relevant demographic and clinical data will also be collected from medical records.
conditions: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Crohn's Disease and Ulcerative Colitis)
primary_outcomes: Change in kinesiophobia level
title: Effects of Different Physical Activity Strategies on Disease Activity of IBD Patients

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether ChronoCoach, a nurse-led multidisciplinary digital coaching program, improves blood sugar control and self-management in adults with type 2 diabetes attending primary health care diabetes services in Bahrain. The main question it aims to answer is: Does ChronoCoach plus usual care lower HbA1c more than usual care alone after 3 months? Researchers will also compare diabetes self-care, self-efficacy, family involvement, quality of life and satisfaction, and will explore feasibility and acceptability.

Participants will be randomly assigned to ChronoCoach or usual care. ChronoCoach participants will use a smartphone app for 3 months to record blood glucose, medicines, symptoms, food and activity, and will receive structured coaching from a diabetes nurse with pharmacy, nutrition, exercise, psychological and physician input when needed. All participants continue usual care and complete HbA1c testing and questionnaires at baseline, 3 months and 6 months.

Research hypothesis:

\* Participants allocated to ChronoCoach will have a greater reduction in HbA1c than participants receiving usual care, after adjusting for baseline HbA1c.
primary_outcomes: Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c)
title: A Nurse-Led Digital Coaching Program to Improve Blood Sugar Control in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary:
Some patients presenting with visual symptoms may have difficulty accurately describing their visual experiences. Symptoms such as blurred vision, diplopia, visual field deficits, and transient visual disturbances are subjective and can be challenging to communicate using words alone. This can create communication barriers and contribute to variability in symptom interpretation, with potential implications for reduced patient satisfaction and uncertainty in clinical evaluation, especially among medical trainees.

This prospective, survey-based feasibility and usability study will have the primary objective of evaluating whether a visual symptom simulator (VSS) improves communication of visual symptoms during neuro-ophthalmology assessment compared with standard history-taking alone, and whether it can be feasibly integrated into routine clinical practice as an adjunct to standard history-taking.

Secondary objectives include: 1) assessing whether the use of a visual simulator improves the clarity of patient-reported visual symptoms and reduces ambiguity during clinical assessment; and 2) exploring its potential role in improving trainees' (medical students, residents, fellows) understanding and interpretation of subjective visual symptoms in neuro-ophthalmology.
primary_outcomes: Patient survey scores
title: Visual Symptom Simulator

brief_summary: Metabolic syndrome is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes, and its prevalence in young adults is increasing. Early identification of individuals at risk may improve prevention strategies. This observational, cross-sectional case-control study investigates the relationship between serum asprosin concentration, the expression of six selected circulating microRNAs, and the components and risk factors of metabolic syndrome in young women aged 18 to 35 years. Two equally sized groups will be compared: women meeting NCEP ATP III criteria for metabolic syndrome and healthy age-matched controls. Participants attend a single study visit during which fasting blood samples, anthropometric and body composition measurements, blood pressure, and validated questionnaires assessing physical activity, diet, sleep quality, perceived stress, and quality of life are collected. The study aims to determine whether asprosin and the selected microRNA profile have diagnostic value as biomarkers of metabolic syndrome in this population.
lead_sponsor: University of Applied Sciences in Nowy Targ
primary_outcomes: Serum asprosin concentration
Expression of selected circulating microRNAs
title: Asprosin and miRNA Expression in Young Women With Metabolic Syndrome

brief_summary: This prospective, multicenter diagnostic accuracy study will evaluate whether POSLUMA (flotufolastat F 18) PET/MRI or PET/CT can detect clinically significant prostate cancer, defined as Gleason score 7 or higher, in adult men with PI-RADS 3 lesions on recent multiparametric MRI and a clinical indication for prostate biopsy. Participants will undergo a research-only POSLUMA PET scan before targeted and systematic prostate biopsy. PET imaging metrics and clinical variables will be compared with histopathology. Research PET results will not be used to guide clinical management or replace standard diagnostic procedures.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of POSLUMA PET for clinically significant prostate cancer
title: POSLUMA PET Imaging for PI-RADS 3 Prostate Lesions

brief_summary:
This study evaluates two ultrasound-guided nerve block techniques-Erector Spinae Plane Block (ESPB) and Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) block-for pain relief in children undergoing elective open inguinal hernia repair.

Children aged 2 to 8 years scheduled for unilateral open inguinal hernia surgery under general anesthesia will be randomly assigned to receive either a lumbar ESP block or a TAP block before surgery begins. Both groups will receive standardized pain management with non-opioid pain relievers (paracetamol and ibuprofen).

The main goal of the study is to compare how long each nerve block provides effective pain relief before the child requires additional pain medication (rescue opioid) within the first 24 hours after surgery. The study will also assess overall pain scores, total opioid consumption, postoperative recovery, and safety.

brief_summary:
Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the top cause of death worldwide . While guideline-directed medical therapy forms the foundation of CAD treatment , revascularization via percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery is critical for complex cases, such as multivessel disease or acute coronary syndromes (ACS). Post-procedure, patients are classified as having achieved complete revascularization (CR) or incomplete revascularization (ICR). The residual SYNTAX score (rSS) objectively quantifies this leftover stenosis, where higher scores predict worse long-term outcomes .

Concurrently, inflammation heavily drives ACS pathogenesis, plaque instability, and residual cardiovascular risk . Complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices - specifically NLR, PLR, SII, and MLR - offer inexpensive, accessible markers of this systemic inflammatory status .

The Knowledge Gap: Most research evaluates rSS alongside traditional risk factors, ignoring systemic inflammation in a unified prognostic framework. Existing studies on these CBC indices often focus broadly on STEMI or general PCI populations, rather than isolated ICR patients. Furthermore, they rely on single measurements, failing to evaluate the incremental value or dynamic changes (baseline vs. post-procedural) of these indices over rSS alone.

Study Hypotheses: This study hypothesizes that baseline, 24-hour post-PCI, and dynamic changes in NLR, PLR, SII, and MLR are independently associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in angiographically documented ICR patients. Ultimately, adding these inflammatory indices to the rSS will significantly improve MACE prognostic discrimination, yielding superior AUC, NRI, and IDI values compared to using rSS alone.

Primary aim: To determine whether the addition of baseline and post-PCI CBC-derived inflammatory indices (NLR and SII) to rSS improves discrimination for MACE compared with rSS alone.

Secondary aims:

1. To determine whether the addition of baseline and post-PCI PLR and MLR to rSS improves discrimination for MACE compared with rSS alone.
2. To assess the correlation between baseline and post-PCI NLR, PLR, SII, MLR and rSS as a continuous variable.
3. To determine whether inflammatory indices are independently associated with MACE after adjustment for demographic, clinical, laboratory, angiographic, and procedural variables.
4. To assess whether changes in NLR, PLR, SII, and MLR from baseline to 24 h post-PCI provide incremental prognostic information beyond static values and rSS.

Patients .

* Patients presenting with STEMI or high risk NSTEMI undergoing Primary PCI and with incomplete revascularization will be included in the study.
* Eligible patients will be subjected to the following:

I- History taking and examination 2-After completion of the index PCI, Incomplete revascularization will be defined as the presence of significant residual coronary artery disease, resulting in a rSS \>0 . .

3-A baseline CBC will be obtained immediately after admission, before coronary angiography/PCI . second CBC will be obtained (24±2 hours) after PCI, the interval between PCI and 2nd CBC sampling will be recorded The following indices will be calculated: NLR = absolute Neutrophil count\\ Absolute Lymphocyte count, PLR = Platelet count\\Absolute Lymphocyte count, SII = Platelets count x neutrophils count \\ lymphocytes count and MLR = Monocytes count \\lymphocytes count.

4-Peak troponin or CK-MB will be recorded after 12-24 hours of onset of symptoms and used as a surrogate measure of infarct size and included as a covariate in the multivariable analysis.

5-Transthoracic echocardiography will be performed by cardiologists blinded to the study within the first 24hr after PCI according to current practice guidelines 5-Patients will be followed for 12 months after the index PCI. 6-The primary endpoint will be the occurrence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) during follow-up in the form of Cardiovascular death due to new ischemic event, Non-fatal myocardial infarction and Unplanned ischemia-driven repeat coronary revascularization.

Secondary end point: Onset of new ischemic events (UA, worsening of chest pain or ischemic induced heart failure)
primary_outcomes: To determine whether the addition of baseline and post-PCI CBC-derived inflammatory indices (NLR and SII) to rSS improves discrimination for MACE compared with rSS alone by comparing area under curve of rSS combined with NLR and SSI and rSS alone.
title: Incremental Prognostic Utility of CBC-derived Inflammatory Indices After Incomplete Coronary Revascularization: Association With 12-months Cardiovascular Outcomes

brief_summary: More than half of people living with HIV (PWH) in the United States are 50 years of age or older. Older PWH have a 2.3-fold increased risk of depression compared to their peers without HIV. The investigator team has developed a streamlined lay-delivered behavioral activation intervention called "Do More, Feel Better" that has been shown to decrease depressive symptoms among older adults obtaining services in community senior centers. The investigators propose to (1) identify barriers and facilitators to improving mental health among older PWH by using this intervention in the context of Ryan White case management services, (2) adapt and enhance the intervention to meet the needs of older PWH, and (3) conduct a pilot randomized controlled trial to determine the acceptability, feasibility, and appropriateness of the adapted DMFB intervention.
interventions: "Do More, Feel Better" for Older People with HIV
primary_outcomes: Acceptability of Intervention Measure (AIM)
Intervention Appropriateness Measure (IAM)
Feasibility of Intervention Measure (FIM)
Session attendance
Exit interview
title: Adapting the "Do More, Feel Better" Intervention for Older People Living With HIV

brief_summary:
This single-center, retrospective observational study aims to compare the clinical and microbiological characteristics of initial and subsequent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) in intensive care unit (ICU) patients.

The study will retrospectively review clinical records of adult patients admitted to the Anesthesiology and Reanimation Intensive Care Unit of Dr. Abdurrahman Yurtaslan Ankara Oncology Training and Research Hospital between January 1, 2014, and December 31, 2025. Patients aged 18 years or older who stayed in the ICU for at least 48 hours and developed at least one HAI will be eligible for inclusion.

The first HAI diagnosed during the ICU stay will be defined as the index infection, and the first new HAI occurring thereafter will be classified as the subsequent infection. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/National Healthcare Safety Network (CDC/NHSN) 14-day repeat infection timeframe will be considered when identifying distinct infection episodes.

The study will compare clinical characteristics of patients with and without subsequent HAIs. Among patients who develop subsequent infections, changes in infection sites and causative microorganisms will be evaluated, along with the time interval between infection episodes.

All data will be obtained from existing hospital records and infection surveillance databases. No additional diagnostic procedures, treatments, or direct patient contact will be performed.
lead_sponsor: Dr Abdurrahman Yurtaslan Ankara Oncology Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Change in Infection Site Between Index and First Subsequent Healthcare-Associated Infections
Change in Causative Microorganisms Between Index and First Subsequent Healthcare-Associated Infections
title: Initial and Subsequent Healthcare-Associated Infections in Intensive Care Patients

brief_summary: 22 children with two primary molars that need extraction or pulpotomy will be selected to compare pain perception between conventional dental syringe and cordless electronic local anesthetic delivery system.
interventions: Cordless Electronic local anesthetic delivery system
primary_outcomes: Pain perception
title: Pain Perception With Cordless Electronic Local Anesthetic Delivery System

brief_summary:
This randomized study compared absorbable facial lifting threads with and without a hyaluronic acid (HA) coating in 144 adults with moderate-to-severe nasolabial folds, the lines extending from the sides of the nose toward the corners of the mouth. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either HA-coated or non-HA threads.

Follow-up continued for six months. The main assessments evaluated adverse events through Day 30 and changes in nasolabial fold severity at Day 90. Independent evaluators assessed standardized photographs, and participants rated their aesthetic improvement and satisfaction. Additional assessments examined safety and maintenance of improvement through Day 180
interventions: P(LA/CL) lifting threads without HA coating
primary_outcomes: Incidence of device and procedure related serious adverse events by Day 30 (Month 1) after the implantation procedure.
Reduction in NLF severity at Day 90 (Month 3) after the implantation procedure in comparison with baseline grading, as assessed by blinded evaluators using the Wrinkles Severity Rating Scale (WSRS).
title: HA-Coated and Non-HA Threads for Midface Lifting and Nasolabial Fold Correction

brief_summary: This study is a prospective randomized controlled trial aimed at evaluating whether the combination of esketamine and transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) can improve the quality of postoperative recovery in women undergoing elective cesarean section. First-time mothers scheduled for surgery will be randomly assigned to one of four groups: a control group (standard care), a TEAS group, an esketamine group, or a combined group (TEAS plus esketamine). TEAS will be applied to specific acupoints before delivery. Esketamine (0.15 mg/kg) will be administered intravenously immediately after the umbilical cord is clamped to minimize fetal exposure. The primary outcome is the overall quality of recovery, assessed using the ObsQoR-11 scale during the first three days after surgery. We will also evaluate pain levels, sleep quality, anxiety and depression, early recovery milestones, inflammatory responses, adverse reactions, and newborn safety. The results may provide an effective multi-modal strategy to enhance recovery for mothers after a cesarean delivery.
primary_outcomes: Quality of Postoperative Recovery
title: Esketamine Combined With Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation on Postoperative Recovery Quality After Elective Cesarean Section

brief_summary:
This study tests a new, fast blood test that may help detect very small traces of tumor DNA in the bloodstream. When tumor cells die, they release small pieces of DNA called circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) into the blood. Finding these pieces can help doctors diagnose cancer, monitor how well treatment is working, and detect cancer recurrence earlier. However, ctDNA is present in very small amounts and is hard to detect with current methods. Newer techniques such as next-generation sequencing (NGS) can find ctDNA, but they are expensive, require specialized laboratories, and take days to return results. This study evaluates a new testing method called "CRISPR/Cas12a combined with gold nanoparticle detection." This method uses a gene-editing protein (Cas12a) that can recognize a specific mutation in the BRCA1 gene and a gold nanoparticle-based readout that shows results within about 30 minutes, using portable equipment.

The main purpose of this study is to find out how accurate, sensitive, and specific this new test is compared with NGS, which is considered the gold standard. The study will also check whether the portable device works consistently across different hospitals and whether the test results match patients' responses to treatment.

The study will enroll adult cancer patients treated at participating hospitals and a group of healthy volunteers. All participants will provide about 3 mL of blood (less than one teaspoon). No additional invasive procedures or extra hospital visits are required beyond routine blood draws. For cancer patients, part of the blood sample will be tested with the new method and part will be tested with standard NGS, and the two results will be compared. Healthy volunteers' blood will be used to confirm that the test does not produce false positive results.

There is no direct physical harm from the test itself, since it is performed on blood samples in the laboratory. Participants will receive the ctDNA test free of charge, and their test results may help their doctors better understand their disease.

The results of this study may help develop a rapid, low-cost, bedside test for tumor DNA, which could improve cancer diagnosis and monitoring in the future.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of the CRISPR/Cas12a-gold nanoparticle ctDNA test compared with NGS
title: Detection Technology of Peripheral Blood ctDNA Based on CRISPR/Cas and Gold Nanoparticles

brief_summary:
The MAGIC trial is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized (1:1) interventional study designed to evaluate whether drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty guided by computational μFR assessment is superior to conventional angiographic-guided DCB angioplasty in terms of acute physiological outcomes.

The study will enroll approximately 250 patients with de novo lesions in native coronary arteries with a reference vessel diameter (RVD) of 2.0-4.0 mm. Participants will be randomized to one of two treatment strategies.

In the angiography-guided control group, DCB angioplasty will be performed according to conventional angiographic criteria for an optimal procedural result, including TIMI grade 3 flow, residual stenosis of less than 30%, and absence of coronary artery dissections of type C or greater.

In the μFR-guided group, computational μFR will be assessed at baseline, after lesion predilation, and after DCB treatment. Virtual percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) will be recommended to guide and optimize the angioplasty strategy, with the aim of achieving a final μFR value ≥0.86. If the physiological result remains suboptimal (μFR \<0.86) despite further lesion preparation, a hybrid strategy involving implantation of a drug-eluting stent (DES) will be permitted.

The primary endpoint is the proportion of target vessels with a post-procedure μFR value ≥0.86, as assessed by an independent, blinded core laboratory through analysis of final coronary angiograms.

Clinical follow-up will be conducted exclusively by telephone over a total period of 24 months.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Target Vessels With Post-Procedure μFR ≥0.86
Incidence of Major Clinical Safety Events at 30 Days
title: Computational μFR-Guided Versus Angiographic Guidance in Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty

brief_summary:
Background: The central nervous system (CNS) recurrence rate of patients with high-risk diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is as high as 15% - 20%, and the prognosis is extremely poor once it occurs. Current intrathecal injection and high-dose methotrexate prophylaxis are ineffective and have significant toxicity. Lenalidomide, BTK inhibitors, and sidaribine all can penetrate the blood-brain barrier, and each has shown a signal of reducing the risk of CNS recurrence in previous studies, but there is still a lack of prospective concurrent comparative data.

Objective: To preliminarily evaluate the efficacy and safety of using these three oral drugs (lenalidomide, BTK inhibitors, and sidaribine) in combination with first-line immunotherapy chemotherapy for high-risk DLBCL patients to prevent CNS recurrence during the same period or after chemotherapy.

Method: This study is a phase II exploratory, open-label, non-randomized concurrent multi-cohort study, combined with historical external controls. A total of 87 patients with DLBCL diagnosed by histopathology and having at least one CNS high-risk factor (CNS-IPI ≥ 4 points, specific extranodal involvement (such as testis, breast, adrenal gland, kidney, uterus, bone marrow, bone), and extranodal invasion sites ≥ 2) are planned to be enrolled. Patients can choose to enter the lenalidomide group, BTK inhibitor group (ibrutinib, zanubrutinib, or obinutinib) or sidaribine group based on their disease characteristics and economic conditions, and the preventive treatment lasts for 1 year. The primary endpoint is the 2-year cumulative CNS recurrence rate (competitive risk model analysis), and the secondary endpoints include progression-free survival time, overall survival time, CNS disease-free survival time, and safety.

Significance: This study is the first to prospectively compare the CNS preventive value of these three drugs with different mechanisms in high-risk DLBCL patients, which is expected to provide key exploratory data for this field and lay the foundation for future confirmatory studies.
lead_sponsor: Cancer Institute and Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences
primary_outcomes: Two-year cumulative recurrence rate of CNS
title: Prophylactic Strategies for Mitigating Central Nervous System Relapse in Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma

brief_summary:
This prospective, multicenter, randomized, parallel-group, open-label, noninferiority study compares the safety and efficacy of the Compound Steep-Pulse Therapy Apparatus with radiofrequency ablation in adults with malignant liver tumors. Eligible participants are randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the test group or the control group using a web-based central randomization system, with stratification by tumor diameter and tumor type.

The primary outcome is the ablation success rate at 1 month after treatment, assessed by contrast-enhanced computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging under blinded conditions. Secondary outcomes include ablation success at 3 months, complete ablation rates, tumor response, local recurrence-free rates, procedure-related complications, console operability, and system stability. Safety is evaluated through adverse events and laboratory assessments.
primary_outcomes: Ablation success rate at 1 month after ablation

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether accelerated transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), in which two sessions of stimulation are delivered within a single day, can immediately improve leg muscle strength in physically inactive college students. tDCS is a non-invasive technique that applies a weak, constant electrical current through electrodes on the scalp to change the excitability of the brain area under the electrode. In this study, stimulation targets the leg area of the primary motor cortex.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does a single application of accelerated tDCS or single-session tDCS improve maximal strength, explosive strength and muscular endurance of the knee muscles more than sham stimulation?
* Does dividing stimulation into two 10-minute sessions separated by 3 or 20 minutes produce larger immediate effects than one 10-minute or one 20-minute session?

Researchers will compare five groups: two accelerated tDCS groups (two 10-minute sessions separated by 3 or 20 minutes), two single-session tDCS groups (one 10-minute or one 20-minute session) and a sham stimulation group.

Participants will:

* Attend one laboratory visit
* Complete isokinetic strength tests of the knee flexors and extensors of both legs before stimulation
* Receive the assigned stimulation protocol while sitting at rest
* Repeat the same strength tests immediately after stimulation and report any sensations or discomfort related to stimulation
primary_outcomes: Change in Peak Torque of the Knee Flexors and Extensors at 60 Degrees per Second
Change in Average Power of the Knee Flexors and Extensors at 180 Degrees per Second
Change in Work Fatigue of the Knee Flexors and Extensors at 180 Degrees per Second
title: Acute Effects of Accelerated Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation on Leg Muscle Strength in Physically Inactive College Students

brief_summary:
Parents and caregivers play a key role in shaping children's oral health-related behaviours. However, traditional oral health education (OHE) is not engaging for young children. Game-based learning provides an interactive and enjoyable approach that may improve children's interest, motivation, and understanding. Parent-child interactive games may also encourage communication, shared learning, and behaviour reinforcement at home.

Therefore, the proposed study aims to investigate the efficacy of parent-child interactive game (PCIG)-based OHE in promoting oral health among preschool children. A total of 282 children will be recruited from kindergartens. They will be randomly allocated into three groups with a 1:1:1 ratio, and receive the following interventions: i) Conventional OHE for children only; ii) Conventional OHE for children and parents; and iii) Interactive game-based OHE for children and parents.

The primary outcome is children's oral hygiene status, while the secondary outcome is caries status, caries activity, oral health-related behaviours, dental anxiety, and screen time. We anticipate that children in Group 3 will have better oral hygiene status, lower caries incidence, reduced caries activity, more favourable oral health-related behaviours, lower dental anxiety, and less screen time. If proven effective, family-based OHE can be recommended on a large scale to improve oral health at the family level.
primary_outcomes: Oral hygiene
title: Game-based Oral Health Promotion

The Neurofunctional Assessment (NFA) is a global tool, originally developed for preterm infants, that focuses on the development of normal functions and is based on the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) approach. This study focuses on seven postural-motor manoeuvres drawn from the full NFA (squatting, balancing, supine-to-sit righting, ventral suspension, axillary suspension, lateral suspension and guided rolling), which assess three domains: axial control, distal selective motor control and lateral asymmetries.

brief_summary:
Lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration is a common condition that may be associated with chronic low back pain, reduced spinal flexibility, and limitations in daily activities. Changes in the paravertebral muscles and thoracolumbar fascia may also be related to these symptoms. However, the relationships among these structural and functional factors are not fully understood.

The aim of this prospective observational study is to investigate the relationships among disability, flexibility, paravertebral muscle characteristics, and thoracolumbar fascia thickness and morphology in patients with lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration.

The study will include female patients aged 20-75 years with low back pain accompanied by radiating leg pain lasting at least 3 months. Participants will undergo clinical assessments of pain, disability, and lumbar flexibility. Ultrasonography will be used to evaluate thoracolumbar fascia thickness and morphological characteristics, as well as paravertebral muscle trophism. Previously acquired lumbar magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans will be reviewed to assess intervertebral disc degeneration, the presence or absence of lumbar disc herniation, and paravertebral muscle characteristics, including fatty infiltration.

The study aims to improve the understanding of the relationships between lumbar spine structural changes, surrounding musculoskeletal tissues, pain, disability, and flexibility. No experimental treatment will be assigned to participants.

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, single-arm, interventional clinical study. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of Photodynamic Therapy (PDT) combined with a self-expandable radioactive particle-loaded biliary stent in patients with unresectable extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

Patients diagnosed with extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma who are unable to undergo surgical resection will be enrolled. After initial percutaneous transhepatic cholangial drainage (PTCD) to improve liver function, patients will receive an intravenous injection of a photosensitizer (Hematoporphyrin, 3 mg/kg). Approximately 48-72 hours later, PDT will be performed under DSA guidance (1-2 sessions). Subsequently, a self-expandable biliary stent loaded with Iodine-125 radioactive particles will be implanted into the stricture to maintain biliary patency and provide local brachytherapy.

The primary outcome is tumor response or biliary patency evaluated by RECIST v1.1. Secondary outcomes include overall survival, stent patency duration, changes in liver function and tumor markers, and incidence of adverse events. This study aims to provide a new, effective treatment strategy for unresectable extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
primary_outcomes: Tumor response and biliary patency evaluated by RECIST v1.1
title: Photodynamic Therapy Combined With a Self-expandable Radioactive Particle-loaded Biliary Stent for Unresectable Extrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma

brief_summary: Plantar fasciitis is one of the most common causes of heel pain encountered in musculoskeletal and orthopedic physiotherapy practice. It is characterized by degenerative changes at the origin of the plantar fascia on the medial calcaneal tubercle, leading to pain, stiffness, and functional limitations during weight-bearing activities. Patients typically report sharp heel pain that is most severe during the first steps in the morning or after prolonged rest, which significantly affects gait and daily functional activities.Current evidence suggests that plantar fasciitis is not purely an inflammatory condition but rather a degenerative fasciopathy resulting from repetitive microtrauma, abnormal foot biomechanics, prolonged standing, obesity, and tightness of the gastrosoleus complex. These mechanical stressors lead to microtears, collagen degeneration, and thickening of the plantar fascia, ultimately resulting in chronic pain and disability.Objective of this study is to compare the effectiveness of Active Release Technique and Dynamic Soft Tissue Mobilization on pain, function, and disability in patients with plantar fasciitis. All the subjects who will eligible for the criteria will randomly allocated in to Group A(ART) and Group B(DSTM).Taping will be our baseline treatment.. This study will be a randomized controlled trial conducted at Pro Care Physiotherapy Clinic, Ittefaq Hospital, and Iffat Anwar Medical Complex over a period of four months. A total of 62 participants will be recruited using probability convenient sampling and randomly allocated into two groups. Group A will receive Active Release Technique along with baseline taping, while Group B will receive Dynamic Soft Tissue Mobilization along with baseline taping. Both groups will receive three sessions per week for four weeks.Outcome measures will include the Numerical Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) and Foot Function Index (FFI) to assess pain and functional disability. Assessments will be taken at baseline, 2nd week, and 4th week. Data will be analyzed using SPSS version 24, and both intra-group and inter-group comparisons will be performed using appropriate statistical tests.

brief_summary:
Introduction : Androgens play a vital role in the female reproductive system, influencing ovarian follicular development, oocyte quality, and ovarian responsiveness to controlled ovarian stimulation. The main circulating androgens include dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S), dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), androstenedione (AD), testosterone (T), and dihydrotestosterone (DHT). Studies have shown that androgens promote early follicular growth by regulating follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) receptor expression and the intrafollicular microenvironment; however, excessive levels may interfere with follicular maturation and ovulation, leading to ovarian dysfunction. Total testosterone (TT) represents the sum of bound and free circulating testosterone. The majority of circulating testosterone is tightly bound to sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) or loosely bound to albumin (ALB), α-globulins, and corticosteroid-binding globulin, with only 1-4% existing as free testosterone (FT). Only free testosterone can enter cells and exert biological effects. Because SHBG concentrations are readily influenced by sex, age, body weight, metabolic syndrome, SHBG gene polymorphisms, and certain medications, whereas FT is unaffected by SHBG, FT is considered an ideal marker for assessing bioactive testosterone status. Free testosterone, as the most biologically active androgen form, is closely correlated with ovarian response, particularly in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).

Mass spectrometry （LC-MS/MS）is widely recognized as a highly accurate method for determining androgen profiles. However, due to various factors such as cost, large-scale studies using mass spectrometry to measure androgen profiles have not yet been conducted, and there is even a lack of research on the diagnostic performance of mass spectrometry-derived androgen profiles for polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).

The aim of this study is to evaluate the diagnostic performance (AUC, sensitivity, and specificity) of LC-MS/MS-measured androgen profiles in a multicenter real-world cohort for PCOS diagnosis. We will compare the diagnostic value of DHEA-S, DHEA, AD, T, DHT, and FT, and develop a multi-marker combined diagnostic model using machine learning to optimize the diagnostic efficacy for PCOS.

The primary research question is: Can LC-MS/MS-measured androgen profiles improve the diagnostic accuracy for PCOS?

By recruiting an appropriate number of participants and measuring the above serum biomarkers, we will statistically analyze the diagnostic performance of LC-MS/MS-determined androgen profiles, especially free testosterone (FT), in PCOS.
lead_sponsor: Women's Hospital School Of Medicine Zhejiang University
primary_outcomes: Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) of LC-MS/MS-derived Androgen Profiles for the Diagnosis of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) of LC-MS/MS-derived Androgen Profiles for the Diagnosis of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
title: The Value of LC-MS/MS Detection of Androgen Profiles in the Diagnosis of PCOS: A Prospective, Multicenter Real-world Study
