brief_summary:
This study aims to compare high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) with conventional nasal cannula oxygen during sedation for combined upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy (gastroscopy and colonoscopy) in patients aged 75 years and older.

Sedation is commonly used during gastrointestinal endoscopic procedures to improve patient comfort. However, sedative medications may cause respiratory depression and hypoxemia. Conventional nasal cannula oxygen is routinely used to provide supplemental oxygen, whereas high-flow nasal oxygen delivers heated and humidified oxygen at higher flow rates and may help maintain oxygenation during sedation. The effectiveness of high-flow nasal oxygen in older patients undergoing gastroscopy and colonoscopy during the same session requires further evaluation.

In this randomized controlled study, eligible patients will be assigned to one of two groups. In the high-flow nasal oxygen group, preoxygenation will be administered for 3 minutes at a flow rate of 40 L/min with an inspired oxygen fraction (FiO₂) of 50%. Once the target sedation level is achieved, the flow rate will be increased to 60 L/min, with FiO₂ maintained at 50%, and oxygen support will continue until the end of the procedure. In the conventional nasal cannula group, oxygen will be administered at a flow rate of 6 L/min for 3 minutes before sedation and continued throughout the procedure. Patients in both groups will maintain spontaneous breathing.

The primary outcome is the occurrence of hypoxemia, defined as peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂) below 90% for at least 10 seconds during sedation and endoscopy. SpO₂ will be continuously monitored throughout the procedure. Secondary outcomes include the minimum SpO₂, total duration of hypoxemia, apnea episodes, the need for airway or ventilation interventions, changes in hemodynamic parameters, sedative and analgesic medication requirements, procedure duration, and adverse events. Any rescue interventions performed in response to hypoxemia or respiratory compromise will be recorded.

The study will evaluate whether high-flow nasal oxygen reduces the incidence of hypoxemia compared with conventional nasal cannula oxygen in patients aged 75 years and older undergoing combined upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy under sedation. The findings may help inform oxygen supplementation strategies for this older patient population.
lead_sponsor: Turkish Society of Anesthesiology and Reanimation
primary_outcomes: Hypoxemia
title: HFNC vs Conventional Oxygen During Gastrocolonoscopy in Elderly Patients

brief_summary:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by progressive joint damage and bone erosion. Accurate assessment of RA bone erosion risk (RABER) and appropriate disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD) selection are critical to preventing irreversible disability.

Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly large language models (LLMs), enable integration of heterogeneous clinical data and may improve clinical decision-making. However, there is limited real-world evidence (RWE) evaluating whether GenAI can meaningfully augment physician decision-making in routine care.

This prospective, single-arm, nonrandomized interventional study evaluates the feasibility and impact of GenAI-assisted clinical decision support on physician assessment of rheumatoid arthritis bone erosion risk and disease-modifying antirheumatic drug selection in routine inpatient care. Treating physicians document their initial risk assessments and treatment decisions before reviewing patient-specific GenAI reports and subsequently record their assessments and decisions after reviewing the reports. The study evaluates changes in physician clinical decision-making within a learning health system framework. Final treatment decisions remain under the responsibility of the treating physicians. The study does not evaluate long-term patient clinical outcomes.
interventions: GenAI-Assisted Clinical Decision Support for RABER Assessment and DMARD Selection
lead_sponsor: Guang'anmen Hospital of China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With a Change in Physician-Assessed Rheumatoid Arthritis Bone Erosion Risk Level After GenAI-Assisted Decision Support
Cohen's Kappa Agreement Between Physician-Assessed Rheumatoid Arthritis Bone Erosion Risk Levels and the Reference Standard Before and After GenAI-Assisted Decision Support
title: GenAI-Assisted Rheumatoid Arthritis Bone Erosion Risk Assessment and DMARD Selection

brief_summary:
This Phase 3 study is designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-daily roflumilast cream 0.3% in children, adolescents, and adults with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis. Approximately 415 participants will be randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive roflumilast cream 0.3% or matching vehicle cream during a 4-week double-blind, vehicle-controlled treatment period.

Following completion of the double-blind treatment period, all participants will enter a 48-week open-label extension and receive roflumilast cream 0.3%. The study will assess the efficacy of roflumilast cream 0.3% in improving signs and symptoms of atopic dermatitis and evaluate its long-term safety and tolerability through Week 52.
primary_outcomes: Achievement of vIGA-AD Success at Week 4
title: Roflumilast Cream 0.3% for Moderate to Severe Atopic Dermatitis

brief_summary:
This multicenter randomized controlled trial evaluates whether internal mammary node irradiation (IMNI) improves oncologic outcomes in patients with breast cancer who have residual pathologically positive lymph nodes after neoadjuvant systemic therapy.

Eligible participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive locoregional radiotherapy either with or without irradiation of the internal mammary lymph nodes. The primary outcome is disease-free survival. Secondary outcomes include overall survival, breast cancer mortality, locoregional recurrence-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, and treatment-related toxicity, particularly cardiac and pulmonary toxicity.

A total of 1,760 participants are planned to be enrolled across multiple centers in Thailand.

Locoregional Radiotherapy Without Internal Mammary Node Irradiation
primary_outcomes: Disease-Free Survival (DFS)

brief_summary:
The SOFIA study evaluates a web-based health application for people living with one or more chronic conditions. The study aims to find out whether the SOFIA application is useful, easy to use, and used over time by participants.

The SOFIA application offers tools to support the day-to-day management of health: lifestyle challenges, health data entry and personal tracking (e.g., blood pressure, weight), medication tracking for people using pochettes-doses (pharmacy-prepared unit-dose packets), and an AI conversational assistant providing general health information. The application does not make diagnoses, give personalized medical advice, or recommend treatment. It complements usual medical care but does not replace it.

The study first enrolls people with hypertension, then, subject to ethics committee approval, people with type 2 diabetes and obesity.

Participation takes place entirely online, through the SOFIA application, accessible from a web browser (smartphone, tablet, or computer). There are no in-person visits. Participants use the application freely, at their own pace, until the end of the study. Short questionnaires (most take 1 to 3 minutes) are offered in the application during the study, and a final questionnaire (about 20 minutes) at the end.
primary_outcomes: User Retention: Proportion of Participants With Sustained Inactivity (Attrition)
Acceptability: French System Usability Scale (F-SUS) Score
title: Use and Acceptability of an AI-Assisted Health Application for Individuals Living With a Chronic Condition

brief_summary:
This prospective, single-center, non-randomized study with a historical control group evaluated the clinical utility of indocyanine green-guided lymphatic mapping (ICG-LM) during minimally invasive surgery for sigmoid colon and rectal cancer.

Adequate lymph node removal is an essential component of colorectal cancer surgery, as the number of lymph nodes examined influences the accuracy of pathological staging and subsequent treatment decisions. Current oncological recommendations generally support the examination of at least 12 lymph nodes for adequate nodal assessment.

Indocyanine green is a fluorescent dye that enables visualization of lymphatic drainage pathways using near-infrared imaging. Fluorescence-guided lymphatic mapping may help surgeons identify lymphatic structures and lymph nodes that are not readily visible under conventional imaging.

Patients prospectively enrolled in the intervention group underwent endoscopic submucosal injection of ICG before minimally invasive oncological resection. Intraoperative near-infrared fluorescence imaging was used to visualize lymphatic drainage and guide lymph node identification. Outcomes were compared with those of a historical control group of patients who had undergone standard minimally invasive surgery without fluorescence-guided lymphatic mapping.

The primary outcome was the adequacy of lymphadenectomy, evaluated by the proportion of patients with fewer than 12 lymph nodes retrieved and identified during histopathological examination.

Additional outcomes included the total number of retrieved lymph nodes, metastatic lymph node yield, operative time, and postoperative outcomes.

Propensity score matching and overlap weighting were used to account for differences in baseline characteristics between the intervention and historical control groups.

The study assessed the potential value of ICG-guided lymphatic mapping for improving lymph node assessment during minimally invasive surgery for sigmoid colon and rectal cancer.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Patients With Inadequate Lymphadenectomy
title: Indocyanine Green Lymphatic Mapping in Minimally Invasive Sigmoid and Rectal Cancer Surgery

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate whether frailty before surgery is associated with difficulty providing adequate breathing support through a face mask after the start of general anesthesia in patients aged 60 years and older undergoing elective cardiac surgery.

Frailty describes reduced physical reserves and an increased vulnerability to health-related stress. Before surgery, participants will be assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale, and handgrip strength will be measured using a handheld dynamometer. These assessments will be evaluated alongside routine patient characteristics and airway measurements.

During routine anesthesia care, the research team will record how effectively patients can be ventilated through a face mask during the first 20 breaths after anesthesia induction. The team will also record the need for additional airway support and any difficulty placing the breathing tube.

The main objective is to assess the association between preoperative frailty and suboptimal mask ventilation. Additional objectives are to assess the association between handgrip strength and suboptimal mask ventilation, whether handgrip strength adds predictive information beyond frailty assessment, and the relationship between suboptimal mask ventilation and intubation difficulty.

This is a single-center, prospective observational study at Ankara Bilkent City Hospital. The study will not change participants' routine anesthesia or surgical care.
interventions: Mask Ventilation During Routine Anesthesia Induction
primary_outcomes: Association Between Preoperative Frailty and Suboptimal Mask Ventilation in Patients Aged 60 Years and Older Undergoing Elective Cardiac Surgery
title: Preoperative Frailty and Suboptimal Mask Ventilation in Cardiac Surgery Patients

brief_summary: The purpose of this research study is to evaluate whether a smartphone-enabled EEG (electroencephalography) system can be used to detect Cognitive Motor Dissociation (CMD) in patients with acute neurological injuries who appear unable to follow commands at the bedside. CMD occurs when a person may be conscious and able to understand instructions but cannot physically respond. The study will also examine whether CMD detection is associated with short-term and long-term recovery outcomes.

brief_summary: This study will evaluate whether a generative artificial intelligence (AI)-based rehabilitation support system can help older adults with lung cancer recover after lung surgery. Eligible participants aged 65 years or older who are scheduled for video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) will be randomly assigned to receive either personalized perioperative rehabilitation guidance through the AI-based system or usual rehabilitation guidance. The system will provide guidance on exercise, nutrition, and psychological well-being before surgery and during recovery, and participants may report symptoms for follow-up guidance. The study will compare lung function and quality of life between the groups. It will also assess exercise tolerance, emergency department visits, hospital readmissions, and events related to use of the system.

brief_summary:
Patient safety aims to reduce risks during healthcare delivery, prevent avoidable harm, and minimize the consequences of adverse events. Video-based simulation offers a safe learning environment in which nursing students can apply theoretical knowledge. This study aims to evaluate the effect of video-based simulation on nursing students' self-assessed patient safety competency and patient safety knowledge.

This parallel-group randomized controlled trial will recruit 86 third-year nursing students from the Faculty of Health Sciences at Bartın University during the fall semester of the 2026-2027 academic year, with 43 students in each group.

Inclusion Criteria:

* Being a third-year nursing student actively enrolled in the fifth semester.
* Having a cumulative grade point average of 2.00-4.00 on a 4.00 scale.
* Having no difficulty understanding or speaking Turkish.
* Providing voluntary informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Having previously received structured patient safety training outside the routine nursing curriculum.
* Having graduated from a health vocational high school or an associate degree program in a health-related field.

An independent statistician will conduct stratified randomization based on baseline Patient Safety Knowledge Test scores and cumulative grade point averages. A separate faculty member will administer the intervention in a suitable classroom within the faculty. Triple blinding will involve the researcher, a separate outcome assessor, and a data analyst who is not responsible for randomization. Group identities will remain concealed from these individuals until the prespecified primary analyses are completed. The researcher's access to the simulation administrator panel will also remain restricted during this period. Participants will be informed that everyone will receive the simulation at different times; however, full participant blinding will not be assumed.

The study includes preparation, pilot testing, and main implementation. The educational content, knowledge test, and simulation materials were reviewed by experts and revised accordingly. The simulation was developed with reference to national and international patient safety goals and simulation design standards. Pilot testing involved 10 students for the simulation and 30 students for the data collection tools.

Both groups will receive standardized theoretical patient safety education. The intervention group will additionally complete the video-based simulation, while the control group will receive access after both groups complete their four-week follow-up assessments. Outcomes will be assessed at four time points: before theoretical education, immediately after theoretical education and before simulation, immediately after simulation, and four weeks after the posttest. Control-group assessments will occur at the same time points.

Data collection instruments will include the Descriptive Characteristics Questionnaire, Patient Safety Knowledge Test, Patient Safety Competency Self-Assessment Tool, and Video-Based Simulation Evaluation Form. The primary outcome will be the overall mean competency score, ranging from 1 to 5. The secondary outcome will be the knowledge test score, ranging from 0 to 100. Higher scores indicate better self-assessed competency and greater knowledge, respectively.

Descriptive statistics and repeated-measures analyses will be used to evaluate group, time, and group-by-time effects. The prespecified comparison of change from the video-preintervention assessment to the immediate posttest between groups will assess the immediate additional effect of the simulation. Follow-up assessments will evaluate maintenance of the effect. Effect estimates will be reported with 95% confidence intervals, and missing data will be addressed according to the prespecified analysis plan.
primary_outcomes: Overall Mean Score on the Patient Safety Competency Self-Assessment Tool
Patient Safety Knowledge Test Score
title: SELF-ASSESSMENT AND KNOWLEDGE LEVEL OF NURSING STUDENTS' PATIENT SAFETY COMPETENCY

brief_summary:
Systemic sclerosis can cause the skin of the fingers to become thick and tight, a condition called sclerodactyly. This can make it difficult to bend, straighten, and use the fingers. This study will evaluate whether intradermal injections of hyaluronidase (Amphadase) can improve hand mobility and function and will assess treatment-related side effects.

Approximately 10 adults with systemic sclerosis and sclerodactyly affecting both hands will participate at Stanford University. For each participant, one hand will be randomly selected by coin flip to receive hyaluronidase injections, while the opposite hand will serve as an untreated control. Participants may receive up to four injection sessions at baseline and approximately months 1, 2, and 3. Both hands will receive the same home exercise guidance throughout the study.

Participants will undergo assessments at baseline and months 1, 2, 3, and 6, including hand mobility and skin examinations, hand function questionnaires, and assessment of symptoms and adverse events. Researchers will compare changes between the treated and untreated hands. The investigator performing hand outcome assessments will be blinded to treatment assignment.
primary_outcomes: Different Between Hands in Change From Baseline in Modified Hand Mobility in Scleroderma (mHAMIS) Score
title: Hyaluronidase Injections for Sclerodactyly in Patients With Scleroderma

brief_summary:
Effective local anaesthesia is essential for safe and comfortable dental treatment in children with haemophilia. However, conventional nerve block techniques, particularly inferior alveolar nerve block, carry an increased risk of bleeding and haematoma formation because of their administration into deep tissues. Therefore, alternative local anaesthetic techniques that may reduce the need for deep nerve blocks are of particular importance in this patient population.

Intraosseous anaesthesia has been proposed as a potential alternative to conventional nerve block techniques. Although previous clinical studies have demonstrated promising results in healthy children, its safety and clinical effectiveness in children with haemophilia have not yet been established.

This prospective, single-group, open-label interventional clinical study aims to evaluate the safety and clinical effectiveness of intraosseous anaesthesia during restorative treatment of maxillary and mandibular primary and permanent molars in children aged 4-12 years with haemophilia A or B. Intraosseous anaesthesia will be administered using the SleeperOne 5 computer-controlled local anaesthetic delivery system, without additional systemic haemostatic treatment in children who do not require such treatment following preoperative haematological assessment. Routine prophylactic regimens will remain unchanged.

Safety will be assessed through injection-site bleeding and haematoma evaluations at 1, 2, 4 and 10 minutes and monitoring of adverse events up to 24 hours after the procedure. Clinical effectiveness will be evaluated based on anaesthetic success, pain scores and pulse rate measurements.

Injection-Site Haematoma Occurrence Following Intraosseous Anaesthesia
Maximum Diameter of Injection-Site Haematoma Following Intraosseous Anaesthesia

title: Safety of Intraosseous Anaesthesia in Children With Haemophilia

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, randomized, controlled, multicenter phase II trial evaluating whether circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) methylation-guided adjuvant therapy improves outcomes after R0 resection of colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM). Patients are randomized 1:1 to a ctDNA-guided arm or a conventional-treatment arm, stratified by RAS/BRAF status and primary tumor sidedness.

In the ctDNA-guided arm, postoperative plasma ctDNA methylation testing (mqMSP, 10 tumor-specific methylation markers, 3-day turnaround) is performed at week 1 after surgery. ctDNA-negative patients enter surveillance with ctDNA and imaging every 3 months, with chemotherapy ± targeted therapy triggered upon ctDNA positivity; ctDNA-positive patients start chemotherapy ± targeted therapy, with treatment paused upon ctDNA clearance and restarted upon recurrence, for a maximum cumulative treatment duration of 6 months and no more than 2 restarts. In the conventional arm, investigators choose adjuvant therapy per NCCN/CSCO guidelines, and blood samples are collected but ctDNA results are blinded and not used for treatment decisions.

The primary endpoint is recurrence-free survival (RFS). Secondary endpoints include overall survival, ctDNA positivity rate and its correlation with clinicopathological features, concordance between ctDNA and imaging, lead time of ctDNA in detecting recurrence, secondary NED conversion rate, feasibility and safety of ctDNA-guided dynamic treatment adjustment, ctDNA clearance rate, report turnaround time, patient-reported outcomes (EORTC QLQ-C30/QLQ-CR29), and health economic evaluation (ICER).
primary_outcomes: Recurrence-Free Survival (RFS)
title: Circulating Tumor DNA Methylation-Guided Adjuvant Therapy Decision-Making in Patients With Resectable Colorectal Cancer Liver Metastases After Resection

brief_summary:
Survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest rarely exceeds 10%, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) started by bystanders is a key factor for survival. Rescue breaths can be a technical and emotional barrier for lay rescuers and are often performed incorrectly, which has led to questioning whether they should be taught in initial basic life support (BLS) training for lay people.

This randomized study compares two BLS and automated external defibrillator (AED) training methods in first-year nursing students at the Universitat Internacional de Catalunya, a population chosen for its similarity to lay first responders. The control group will be trained following the traditional algorithm with chest compressions and mouth-to-mouth rescue breaths (30:2). The intervention group will be trained following a simplified model based only on continuous chest compressions, without rescue breaths.

After training, each participant will complete a theoretical test and an individual simulated cardiac arrest scenario with 8 minutes of uninterrupted CPR on a high-fidelity manikin. Theoretical-practical competence, CPR quality and rescuer fatigue (muscular, cardiovascular and perceived) will be assessed. Competence will be reassessed 4 months later to evaluate retention.

The hypothesis is that BLS and AED training without mouth-to-mouth rescue breaths improves theoretical-practical competence and its retention at 4 months compared with the traditional method during 8 minutes of CPR in lay people.
interventions: BLS and AED Training With Rescue Breaths
BLS and AED Training Without Rescue Breaths
primary_outcomes: Theoretical-Practical Competence Level in Basic Life Support (BLS) and Automated External Defibrillator (AED) After Training
Retention of Theoretical-Practical Competence in BLS and AED
title: Compression-Only Versus Standard Basic Life Support Training in Nursing Students

brief_summary:
HERDA (Holistic, Evidence-based, and cultuRally adapted Depression Adherence) is a pharmacist-led intervention developed to support medication adherence among outpatients with depression in South Kalimantan, Indonesia. It combines structured counseling, behavior change strategies, pharmaceutical care, and culturally adapted educational materials to help patients identify and address difficulties in taking their prescribed medication.

The intervention incorporates the 5A Brief Counseling framework and the Transtheoretical Model (TTM), which guides counseling according to each participant's readiness to change. It also includes screening and a predefined safety pathway for suicide-related concerns, culturally adapted psychoeducation, and family or caregiver engagement when appropriate and with the participant's consent. Cultural, spiritual, and existential considerations are addressed according to individual preferences and within predefined intervention guidelines.

HERDA is delivered by trained pharmacists alongside standard psychiatric care. Participants assigned to the intervention group receive seven planned contacts over approximately four months, combining face-to-face sessions and telephone contacts. Participants assigned to the control group receive standard psychiatric care according to the study protocol.

This randomized controlled trial evaluates whether adding HERDA to standard psychiatric care improves medication adherence among outpatients with depression. The findings are intended to inform the development of evidence-based, culturally responsive pharmacist-led care for people receiving treatment for depression.
primary_outcomes: Medication Adherence Measured by MARS-5
Medication Adherence Measured by Pill Count
title: HERDA: Pharmacist-Led Culturally Adapted Intervention for Depression Medication Adherence

The study will assess changes in patients' insight, medication adherence, and aggressive behaviors before and after the intervention. The findings may help improve nursing care and support recovery and better clinical outcomes among patients with schizophrenia.

brief_summary: Sexual health among young people is an important issue for healthcare professionals, educators, and society. The purpose of this study was to examine the effects of a mobile application on emerging adult men's sexual knowledge, sexual consent, and safer sexual behavior outcomes. A total of 174 emerging adult men were recruited through purposive sampling between November 2022 and July 2023, with 75 in the experimental group and 99 in the control group. Data were collected at three time points: baseline, immediately after the 6-week intervention, and 4 weeks after the intervention ended. The findings showed that the intervention significantly increased sexual knowledge, improved positive attitudes toward sexual consent, and reduced assumptions of consent. It also increased behavioral intentions regarding condom use among participants in committed relationships and improved attitudes toward condom use with casual partners.

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether two inflammatory proteins, interleukin-8 (IL-8) measured in saliva and interleukin-6 (IL-6) measured in blood serum, can help distinguish adults with oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs), such as oral lichen planus and leukoplakia, from adults with healthy oral mucosa, and whether smoking changes these protein levels.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do salivary IL-8 and serum IL-6 levels differ between people with OPMDs and healthy controls, and does this difference depend on smoking status?
* How well do IL-8 and IL-6, alone or combined, discriminate people with OPMDs from healthy controls?

Researchers compared healthy never-smokers, healthy current smokers, never-smokers with OPMDs, and current smokers with OPMDs. An additional exploratory group of current smokers with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) was compared with current smokers with OPMDs.

Participants provided an unstimulated whole saliva sample and a blood sample at a single visit, and completed a clinical, periodontal, and tobacco-use assessment. No treatment was assigned as part of the study.

brief_summary:
This prospective, randomized, assessor-blinded, parallel-group clinical trial aims to compare the effectiveness of early add-on opicapone versus levodopa dose escalation in patients with Parkinson's disease experiencing emerging motor fluctuations.

A total of 46 patients are randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either opicapone 50 mg once daily in addition to their existing dopaminergic treatment or an additional daily dose of levodopa/dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor (100-200 mg).

Treatment effects are assessed over approximately four weeks through standardized clinical evaluations, patient-reported outcome measures, and continuous home-based monitoring using wearable sensors. The primary outcome is the change in daily OFF time objectively estimated by wearable technology. Secondary outcomes include gait performance and variability, motor symptom severity, patient-perceived improvement, quality of life, and treatment safety.

The study aims to determine whether early COMT inhibition provides greater control of motor fluctuations than levodopa dose escalation and to investigate the utility of wearable-derived digital biomarkers for evaluating treatment response under real-world conditions.
primary_outcomes: Change in Wearable-Derived Daily OFF Time
title: Early COMT Inhibition in PD

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether a drop in blood pressure after a meal (postprandial hypotension) and frailty are linked to low blood pressure after the start of general anesthesia (post-induction hypotension) in adults aged 65 years and older having planned non-heart surgery.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do patients whose blood pressure drops after a meal have low blood pressure in the first 20 minutes after the start of anesthesia, or until surgery begins, more often than patients whose blood pressure does not drop?
* Is frailty related to blood pressure drops after a meal and after the start of anesthesia?
* Is the size of the blood pressure drop after a meal related to the size of the blood pressure drop and the need for blood pressure-raising medicines after the start of anesthesia?

Researchers will compare patients with and without postprandial hypotension to see if post-induction hypotension is more common in patients with postprandial hypotension. Researchers will also look at whether patients need intensive care unit admission after surgery and how long they stay in the intensive care unit and in the hospital.

Participants will:

* Have their blood pressure and heart rate measured with an automatic arm cuff before and up to 2 hours after their usual hospital evening meal on the day before surgery
* Answer short questions and complete simple tests for frailty (Edmonton Frail Scale) on the day before surgery
* Answer six short questions about anxiety (Amsterdam Preoperative Anxiety and Information Scale) on the morning of surgery
* Receive their usual anesthesia care; blood pressure values recorded during routine monitoring in the first 20 minutes after the start of anesthesia, or until surgery begins, will be collected for the study
* Have information about intensive care unit admission and length of hospital stay collected from their medical records until discharge
primary_outcomes: Incidence of post-induction hypotension
title: Postprandial Hypotension, Frailty and Post-Induction Hypotension in Older Patients Undergoing Noncardiac Surgery

brief_summary:
Systemic treatments such as chemotherapy or monoclonal antibodies are an essential part of oncological treatment in breast cancer, which have demonstrated a survival benefit (1,2,3,4,5). This cancer is the most common cancer in women, being the cancer with the highest incidence worldwide (6), with an estimated 35,001 new cases in 2023 in Spain (7). This is why a large number of patients receive systemic treatments that help surgery and radiotherapy to achieve a cure of over 80% in our environment, with a 5-year overall survival of 85.5% having been described (7).

These systemic oncological treatments generate well-known skin alterations such as xerosis, pruritus, erythema, pigmentation alterations, papulo-pustular eruptions, dermatosis, and others such as psoriasis (8,9,10,11).

The multimodal treatment of cancer finally becomes a long and hard process which, added to the fear of the diagnosis itself, and the physical changes as a consequence of these treatments, end up reducing the state of mind of the patients who suffer from it (12,13,14).

Self-care and the aesthetic improvement of the patient's appearance are the main reasons for this.

There are aesthetic treatments, such as hyaluronic acid 12mg/ml cross-linked (VYC-12L) in intradermal injection, that could improve the quality and aesthetics of the facial skin, which could help to improve the self-perception of patients who receive it, helping them to recover their self-confidence and improve their quality of life.

Research Question:

To objectively compare the skin quality of patients with previous history of breast cancer who have received and completed treatment with chemotherapy and/or monoclonal antibodies, before and after intradermal injection a cross-linked hyaluronic acid 12mg/ml (VYC-12L) in addition to self-esteem and quality of life.
lead_sponsor: Fundacion para la Formacion e Investigacion Sanitarias de la Region de Murcia
primary_outcomes: Change in Skin Hydration and Elasticity From Baseline
title: Improved Facial Skin Quality and Quality of Life After VYC-12L Treatment in Breast Cancer Survivors

brief_summary:
BACKGROUND \& PURPOSE:

Elderly patients undergoing surgery under general anesthesia are at higher risk for complications when the breathing tube (endotracheal tube) is removed at the end of surgery. Strong coughing or straining during tube removal can cause sudden surges in heart rate and blood pressure, which can lead to complications in older adults with heart or blood vessel conditions.

This study compares two medications placed directly inside the balloon (cuff) of the breathing tube to see which one better prevents coughing and stabilizes blood pressure during tube removal.

WHO CAN PARTICIPATE:

Patients aged 65 to 85 years old who are scheduled for elective non-cardiac surgery under general anesthesia requiring a breathing tube.

STUDY GROUPS \& PROCEDURES:

Participants will be randomly assigned (like flipping a coin) to one of two groups:

1. Group DEX: The breathing tube balloon will be filled with a liquid solution containing dexmedetomidine (a medication that calms breathing airway responses and stabilizes heart rate).
2. Group LIDO: The breathing tube balloon will be filled with alkalinized lidocaine (a numbing medication combined with sodium bicarbonate to help it pass through the tube balloon).

Both medications are designed to seep slowly through the balloon membrane to numb and soothe the airway without entering the bloodstream in large amounts. Neither the patient, the operating room team, nor the researchers evaluating recovery will know which medication is in the tube balloon during surgery.

EXPECTED OUTCOMES:

The primary goal is to measure how many patients experience a "smooth extubation" (defined as having no cough or only a single mild cough) during the first 60 seconds after the breathing tube is removed.

Researchers will also measure blood pressure and heart rate changes before and after tube removal, evaluate recovery quality, and track throat comfort (sore throat or hoarseness) at 1, 6, 12, and 24 hours after surgery.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Smooth Extubation
title: Intracuff Dexmedetomidine Versus Alkalinized Lidocaine for Peri-Extubation Cough and Hemodynamic Responses in Elderly Patients

brief_summary: The overall objective of this proposal is to develop and optimize a CDSS, including several nudges, to increase guideline-concordant statin prescribing for CVD risk (Nudge-CVD-CDSS). Potential nudges will be developed, usability tested and refined and then evaluated in a factorial trial. The aim of this trial is to develop, based on a conceptual model of the prescribing process, a set of potential intervention components (EHR-nudges) to promote and support AHA/ACC guideline-concordant statin prescribing. A user-centered design process will be employed. EHR audit log data will be used to identify technical workflows of current provider prescribing patterns. Provider- and patient-directed default, peer comparison, and salient messaging nudges will be developed (5 total). Patient-directed nudges will encourage patients to prompt their providers to prescribe guideline-concordant statins.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of patients indicated for statin therapy who were prescribed a guideline-approved statin at the correct dose during the study period
title: EHR Nudges: Optimizing a Clinical Decision Support System for Evidence-Based Statin Medication Prescribing to Reduce the Risk of Cardiovascular Disease

brief_summary:
Post-dural puncture headache (PDPH) is a major complication of neuraxial anaesthesia.

Pain is intense, frontal, throbbing, and radiates to the occiput; it is more severe when standing and less severe when lying down.

A lot of studies reported several techniques for management of post-dural puncture headache including conservative, pharmacological or interventional techniques. Conservative techniques such as hydration and bed rest. These therapies aim to decrease CSF loss through the dural hole and restore CSF with additional fluid intake.

Pharmacological treatment such as caffeine , methylxanthine (as theophylline), gabapentinoids, Sumatriptan, cosyntropin, dexamethasone, intravenous (IV) injection of ondansetron and IV opioid were used. Also, there are several interventional treatments like), epidural blood patch greater occipital nerve block, and sphenopalatine ganglion block has been used.

Neostigmine has a biphasic effect on sympathetic ganglia, ie, depolarization followed by hyperpolarization. results in vasoconstriction reflects sympathetic regulation of the blood supply to cerebral vessels . An increase in central acetylcholine can maintain cerebral vasoconstriction Atropine crosses the blood brain barrier and is a parasympatholytic , it increases CSF secretion by antagonizing the effect of acetylcholine on the choroid plexus Gabapentin is an anti-epileptic, similar in structure to the endogenous neurotransmitter gamma-amino-butyric acid, but their exact mechanism for treating PDPH is unclear.

A possible mechanism for gabapentin-mediated analgesia is the modulation of glutamate receptors (N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) and α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) /kainite). Also it inhibits nociceptive responses to intrathecal NMDA and AMPA in vivo.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of postdural puncture headache
title: Oral Gabapentin Versus Intravenous Neostigmine/Atropine Versus Combination of Both for Prevention of PDPH

brief_summary:

This randomized clinical trial included 120 students aged 18-28 years who were enrolled in the Dentistry and Psychology departments at Cyprus Health and Social Sciences University. All participants received the same standardized oral hygiene content, information leaflet, toothbrush, and toothpaste, while the motivational approach differed between groups. Professional scaling and polishing were also performed for all participants. The Silness-Löe Plaque Index (PI) and Löe-Silness Gingival Index (GI) were recorded at baseline and three weeks after the intervention.

The study evaluated changes in plaque and gingival indices to compare the effectiveness of the three motivation methods and assess whether their effects differed between Dentistry and Psychology students.

The study is intended to evaluate the:

* Safety and tolerability of rhPDGF-BB following injections in the infraorbital area
* Preliminary efficacy (responder rate) of rhPDGF-BB compared with placebo
* Effect of different doses of rhPDGF-BB compared with placebo with respect to treatment response and durability
* Pharmacokinetic profile following injection of rhPDGF-BB in the infraorbital region
* Immunogenicity profile following injection of rhPDGF-BB in the infraorbital region

This study will compare two doses of rhPDGF-BB (37.5 µg and 75 µg per infraorbital region) with placebo (normal saline) to evaluate safety and preliminary efficacy of rhPDGF-BB for improving infraorbital hollowing.

Participants will:

brief_summary:
Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is one of the leading causes of preventable visual impairment among working-age adults, with diabetic macular edema (DME) representing one of its most important vision-threatening complications. Diabetic macular edema develops when diabetes-associated retinal vascular dysfunction leads to disruption of the blood-retinal barrier (BRB), allowing fluid and plasma components to accumulate within the retinal tissue and impair macular function. The development and persistence of DME involve a complex interplay between vascular, inflammatory, metabolic, and oxidative mechanisms.

Hyperglycemia is a central driver of the molecular abnormalities underlying diabetic retinal injury. Chronic exposure to elevated glucose activates several interrelated pathways, including the polyol, advanced glycation end-products (AGEs), protein kinase C (PKC), and hexosamine pathways. These metabolic disturbances promote the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), inflammatory signaling, endothelial dysfunction, and progressive impairment of the retinal neurovascular unit. Together, these processes contribute to damage to endothelial cells, pericytes, Müller cells, and other retinal components, ultimately compromising the integrity of the BRB.

Oxidative stress is therefore considered an important component of the pathophysiology of DR and DME. Excessive ROS production can directly damage cellular structures and can also amplify inflammatory and angiogenic signaling. This may increase the expression of several mediators implicated in retinal vascular dysfunction. The resulting vascular instability and increased permeability facilitate fluid extravasation into the retinal layers and contribute to the development and progression of DME.

Malondialdehyde (MDA), a product of lipid peroxidation, is widely used as a marker of oxidative damage. Increased MDA concentrations have been reported in patients with diabetic retinopathy and have been associated with the presence or severity of retinal disease, supporting the involvement of oxidative stress in diabetic retinal injury. Assessment of MDA may therefore provide a useful systemic indicator of the oxidative component of the disease process.

Angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2), an important regulator of vascular stability, has also been implicated in diabetic retinal vascular dysfunction. Increased Ang-2 can promote endothelial destabilization and enhance vascular permeability, particularly in the presence of inflammatory and VEGF-related signaling. Thus, oxidative stress and angiogenic dysregulation may represent interconnected components of the vascular injury that ultimately leads to BRB disruption and retinal fluid accumulation.

Current management of DME relies predominantly on ophthalmic interventions, with corticosteroids and laser photocoagulation having roles in selected clinical settings. Although these approaches have substantially improved visual and anatomical outcomes, persistent or recurrent edema occurs in a proportion of patients, reflecting the multifactorial nature of DME and the involvement of various pathways.

N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is a thiol-containing compound and a precursor of L-cysteine and reduced glutathione. In addition to its established mucolytic properties, NAC has antioxidant activity through direct scavenging of reactive oxygen species and, importantly, through restoration of intracellular glutathione availability. Its ability to modulate oxidative stress has led to extensive investigation of NAC in a variety of clinical conditions characterized by oxidative and inflammatory injury.

Experimental evidence suggests that attenuation of oxidative stress with NAC may reduce diabetes-related retinal injury and suppress the expression of vascular and inflammatory mediators, including VEGF and intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1). However, the potential clinical relevance of oral NAC in patients with diabetic retinal disease remains insufficiently characterized.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Central Subfield Thickness (CST) Measured by Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT)
title: Oral N-Acetylcysteine on Diabetic Macular Edema

brief_summary:
Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and combined metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-associated liver disease (MetALD) are common chronic liver diseases associated with metabolic dysfunction and an increased risk of liver-related and cardiovascular complications. Lifestyle modification, particularly dietary changes and increased physical activity, represents a cornerstone of treatment. However, general lifestyle recommendations are often insufficient to achieve sustained improvements.

This prospective, randomized controlled trial aims to investigate whether personalized dietary and lifestyle feedback based on a structured questionnaire is more effective in reducing hepatic steatosis than generic lifestyle recommendations.

A total of 174 patients with MASLD or MetALD will be randomized 1:1 to receive either personalized or generic written feedback at baseline and after 2, 4, and 6 months. Changes in hepatic steatosis, assessed by the controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), will be evaluated over a six-month period.
primary_outcomes: Hepatic Steatosis at 6 Months, Assessed by Controlled Attenuation Parameter (CAP) Using Vibration-Controlled Transient Elastography (VCTE)
title: Personalized Dietary Feedback to Reduce Hepatic Steatosis in Patients With MASLD

brief_summary:
Adolescent dancers are at high risk of musculoskeletal pain due to repetitive, high-intensity training. Persistent pain may lead to kinesiophobia (fear of movement), which can further impair physical function according to the fear-avoidance model. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) has been used as a top-down intervention for musculoskeletal pain; however, it remains unclear whether its analgesic effect results from true neural stimulation or from contextual factors such as treatment expectation.

This three-arm, single-blind randomized controlled trial will enroll 24 adolescent dancers aged 13 to 18 years with musculoskeletal pain lasting at least 3 months. Participants will be randomly allocated, stratified by pain site, to (1) active tDCS plus manual therapy, (2) sham tDCS plus manual therapy, or (3) sham tDCS plus manual therapy plus structured expectation-enhancement education. Each participant will receive a single intervention session. Outcomes will be assessed before, immediately after, and 1 week after the intervention. The study aims to distinguish the neurophysiological effect of tDCS from the effect of treatment expectation on pain, kinesiophobia, and related outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Change in Pain Intensity (Numeric Pain Rating Scale, NPRS)
title: Effects of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation and Manual Therapy on Musculoskeletal Pain in Adolescent Dancers

In this study, gastric volume will be measured by ultrasonography in the preoperative period in order to investigate whether the fullness of the stomach and gastric volume are related to the predictability of postoperative nausea and vomiting. brief_summary: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common functional gastrointestinal condition characterised by symptoms including abdominal pain or discomfort, bloating, altered bowel habits and changes in digestive comfort. These symptoms can substantially affect quality of life, dietary behaviour, social functioning, and overall wellbeing. Although the underlying mechanisms are complex and multifactorial, growing evidence indicates that the gut microbiota and its interactions with the intestinal environment, immune system, gastrointestinal function, and gut-brain axis may play an important role in gastrointestinal health and symptom development. Prebiotics and probiotics have received increasing attention as nutritional strategies for supporting gut health. Prebiotics are substrates selectively utilised by beneficial microorganisms in the gut and can promote microbial growth and metabolic activity, including the production of short-chain fatty acids that contribute to intestinal barrier function, immune regulation, and colonic health. Probiotics are live microorganisms that, when administered in adequate amounts, may provide health benefits to the host. Selected probiotic strains have been investigated for their potential to support microbial balance, intestinal function, digestive comfort, and immune and inflammatory responses. However, responses to individual prebiotic or probiotic interventions can vary considerably between individuals, highlighting the potential value of complementary or combined nutritional approaches.
primary_outcomes: Changes in gastrointestinal symptom severity
title: Effects of Epetôme on Gastrointestinal Function, Inflammation and Wellbeing in Adults With IBS-like Symptoms (EPEGUT)

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether shear wave elastography (SWE) parameters, combined with dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA), and physical performance assessments, can help diagnose sarcopenia in older adults. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Are SWE-derived muscle stiffness parameters associated with muscle mass, muscle strength, and physical performance?
* Can an integrated model including SWE parameters accurately identify sarcopenia compared with the DXA-based diagnosis?

Researchers will compare participants with sarcopenia to those without sarcopenia, to see if SWE parameters differ between groups and contribute to sarcopenia prediction.

Participants will:

* Undergo shear wave elastography of selected skeletal muscles
* Receive a DXA scan to measure appendicular skeletal muscle mass
* Receive a BIA measurement of body composition
* Complete muscle strength and physical performance assessments
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of shear wave elastography parameters for sarcopenia
title: Multimodal Assessment of Sarcopenia Using Shear Wave Elastography, Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry, Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis, and Physical Performance Measures

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of a four-week immersive virtual reality (VR)-based tennis training program on executive function in healthy older adults. Forty-five adults aged 60-70 years with no previous tennis experience were screened, and 39 eligible participants were randomly assigned to either a VR tennis training group (n = 20) or a VR documentary-viewing control group (n = 19). Thirty-eight participants completed the study (VR tennis group, n = 20; documentary-viewing group, n = 18). The VR tennis group completed tennis training using an HTC Vive head-mounted display and a VR tennis game, while the control group watched VR documentaries using an HTC Vive head-mounted display without engaging in tennis training. Both groups participated in three sessions per week for four weeks. Executive function was assessed at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and one week after the intervention using the Flanker task (inhibitory control), the More-Odd shifting task (cognitive flexibility), and the Corsi block-tapping task (visuospatial working memory). The study compared changes in these executive function measures between the VR tennis training group and the VR documentary-viewing control group.

brief_summary:
This non-interventional study aims to assess the impact of an endometriosis diagnosis obtained through a salivary test (Ziwig Endotest®) on pain-related cognitions, quality of life, mood, and treatment adherence, comparingthese outcomes with those of individuals who underwent the same salivary test but received a negative result and were therefore not diagnosed with endometriosis.

The investigators hope to enhance understanding of endometriosis and pelvic pain symptomatology in order to develop new therapeutic strategies, including psychological interventions or integrated psychological care, that better address the needs and specific characteristics of patients whether or not they receive a diagnosis of endometriosis.

brief_summary: The investigators propose to conduct a prospective study evaluating the prevalence of SNN in pSS patients and to find clinical characteristics and specific immunological profiles in pSS patients with SFN. Peripheral nervous system involvement account for 15% of pSS cases. Among peripheral nervous system complication, SFN appears to be prevalent. However the association between pSS and SFN has been scarcely evaluated. There are not many relevant studies using similar methodology to evaluate pSS patients for small fiber dysfunction. Furthermore, autoimmune mechanisms are thought to play a key role in SFN pathogenesis in pSS and the association between SFN and specific immunological profiles has been poorly studied. So the aim of this study is to evaluate the prevalence of SFN in pSS patients by using the Sudoscan which is a fast and non- invasive tool. The Sudoscan could offer an accessible alternative for early SFN detection, improving patient management. The secondary purpose is to analyze systemic and immunological profiles, as well as disease's activity and quality of life of patients with pSS-related SFN.
primary_outcomes: prevalence of SFN in patients with pSS

brief_summary:
This study will develop and test an artificial intelligence (AI) model that estimates the risk of type 2 diabetes among senior (third- and fourth-year) nursing students at the Faculty of Nursing, Alexandria University, Egypt. Type 2 diabetes is common in Egypt, and many cases are not diagnosed. Daily habits such as diet, physical activity, and body weight play a major role in who develops it. Nursing students will become health care providers who teach patients about healthy living, so it is important to find those who may be at risk early.

About 200 students will take part. Each student will complete a questionnaire about personal information and the Health-Promoting Lifestyle Profile II, which measures health habits such as nutrition, physical activity, stress management, and health responsibility. The researcher will measure height, weight, waist size, and blood pressure. Each student's diabetes risk will be scored using the Arabic version of the Australian Type 2 Diabetes Risk Assessment Tool (AUSDRISK), which classifies risk as low, moderate, or high.

These data will be used to build a machine learning model that predicts each student's diabetes risk level from lifestyle and body measurement factors, and shows which factors influenced the prediction most. Students will then try the model and rate how useful and easy to use it is.

No treatment or intervention will be given. The study aims to support early identification of students at risk and to provide a model that nursing education programs and community health nurses could use in preventive health efforts.
